That is because in the Jāhiliyyah, when a daughter was born to one of them, he kept her in humiliation, or buried her alive in the dust."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿And for them is what they desire﴾, he said: "It refers to sons."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Or does he bury it in the dust﴾, he said: "He buries his daughter alive."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge﴾, he said: "Evil is what they judged. He says: a thing they do not approve for themselves, so how would they approve it for Me?"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "It is the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "He says: there is nothing like Him."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿He has not left upon it any creature﴾, he said: "(i.e., He did not) give them rain."

He also transmitted from al-Suddī something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse, he said: "This was done in the time of Noah. Allah destroyed everything upon the surface of the earth of creatures, except what was carried in His ark."

Aḥmad in *al-Zuhd* transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "The sins of the son of Adam killed the dung beetle in its hole." Then he said: "By Allah, (this was) at the time of the drowning of the people of Noah."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from him: "The dung beetle was almost punished in its hole for the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted something similar from Anas.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, Ibn Jarīr, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from Abū Hurayrah that he heard a man say: "Indeed, the wrongdoer harms only himself." Abū Hurayrah said: "Yes, by Allah, indeed the bustard dies of emaciation in its nest because of the oppression of the oppressor."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk regarding ﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike﴾, he said: "They assign to Me daughters, and they dislike that for themselves."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best﴾, he said: "The statement of the disbelievers of Quraysh to us: 'For us are the sons, and for Him are the daughters.'"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah something similar.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾, he said: "Forgotten."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah, who said: "Hastened."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 16, verses 51–68 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glory be to Him, made clear that His created beings, both celestial and terrestrial, are subject to Him and humbled before His majesty, He followed this with a prohibition of association (shirk) in His words: ﴿And Allah said, "Do not take two gods. He is but one God."﴾ So He forbade taking two gods, then affirmed that divinity (al-ilahiyyah) is confined to one God, who is Allah, glory be to Him. It has been said that the dual form in "two gods" (ilahayn) indicates duality, and the singular in "God" (ilah) indicates unity. So what is the reason for describing "two gods" with "two" (ithnayn), and describing "God" with "one" (wahid)? The answer given is that there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir, rearrangement of words) in the speech, and the sense is: "Do not take two gods; He is only one God." It has also been said that the repetition is for the sake of emphasis in warning against taking a partner. It has also been said that the benefit of adding "two" is to make known that the prohibition concerns plurality and not the kind, and the benefit of adding "one" is to repel the supposition that the intent is only to affirm divinity without oneness, even though divinity itself is conceded to Him, glory be to Him, and the disagreement of the polytheists concerns only His oneness.

Then, by way of iltifat (shift from third person to first person), He, glory be to Him, moved the speech from the third person to the first person in order to increase the intimidation, saying: ﴿So it is Me that you should fear.﴾ That is: if you fear anything, then fear Me alone, not anyone else. The like of this has already passed at the beginning of al-Baqarah.

Then, when He had established His oneness, and that He is the One who must be singled out with fear and with hope directed to Him, He mentioned that all things are in His possession and under His disposal, saying: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This sentence confirms what came earlier in His words: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ (al-Nahl 49), to its end. The placing of the predicate first (taqdim al-khabar) serves to indicate exclusivity. ﴿And for Him is religion, constant.﴾ That is: established, obligatory, perpetual, not ceasing. Religion here means obedience and sincerity. Al-Farra' said: "wasiban" means "perpetual." From this is the verse of Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali:

I do not seek praise whose endurance is brief,
at the price of blame that lasts the whole age, perpetual.

That is: perpetual.

It is also narrated from al-Farra' that he said: "al-wasib" means "the sincere." But the first (meaning) is preferable. From this is His statement: ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾ (al-Saffat 9), that is, lasting.

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, obedience to Him is obligatory forever. Thus he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the obligatory."

Ibn Qutaybah said, in interpreting "al-wasib": no one is obeyed except that this (obedience) ceases through departure or destruction, except Allah, the Exalted, for obedience to Him endures. So he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the enduring." When a thing endures without ceasing, it becomes binding and established. It is said: "wasaba al-shay'u yasibu wusuban, fahuwa wasib," meaning it lasted; and "wasaba al-rajulu 'ala al-amr," meaning he persisted in it. It has also been said that "al-wasab" is fatigue and weariness, meaning that obedience to Allah, glory be to Him, is obligatory even if the servant becomes weary in it. But this does not suit what is in the verse.

The interrogative in His words: ﴿Then is it other than Allah you fear?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, and it is coordinated with an implied element, as in its counterparts. The meaning is: since religion, that is obedience, is obligatory for Him permanently without ceasing, it is fitting to restrict piety (taqwa) to Him and not to direct it to anyone else.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, bestowed favor upon them by stating that all the blessings in which they live come from Him and not from anyone else. He said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah.﴾ That is: whatever blessings come upon you, of their various kinds, are from Allah, that is, they are from Him. Thus "ma" may be conditional (shartiyyah), and it may also be relative (mawsulah) with the sense of a condition, with "bikum" as its complement. "Min ni'mah" is either a circumstantial element (hal) from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase, or an explanation (bayan) of "ma." His words ﴿then from Allah﴾ are the predicate. If "ma" is conditional, the verb of the condition is elided, that is, "ma yakun" (whatever may be). Blessing is either religious, which is knowledge of the truth for its own sake and knowledge of the good for the sake of acting upon it; or worldly, which is either psychological, physical or external, such as material prosperity and other things. Each of these is a genus under which there are countless kinds, and all of them are from Allah, glory be to Him. So the intelligent person should give thanks to none but Him.

Then He explained the fickleness of the human being after he is immersed in the sea of blessings, saying: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help.﴾ That is: when harm touches you, of any kind, you turn to Allah, glory be to Him, and not to anyone else, humbly seeking its removal, for there is no remover of it but Him. It is said: "ja'ara yaj'aru" in the language of the Arabs, "ju'aran," meaning he raised his voice in humble supplication.

Al-A'sha said, describing a cow:

She circled three times between day and night,
and the reproach was that she should circle and cry out.

Harm (al-durr) means illness, affliction, need, drought, and everything by which a person is harmed.

﴿Then when He removes the harm from you, behold, a group of you associate others with their Lord.﴾ That is: when He removes from you the harm that had befallen you, behold, a group among you, those whose harm has been removed, associate others with their Lord, placing with Him another god, such as an idol or the like. The verse is brought to express wonder at the conduct of these people, who place partnership with Allah, who bestowed favor upon them by removing the harm that had befallen them, in place of gratitude to Him. This meaning has already appeared in al-An'am and Yunus, and will come in al-Isra'.

Al-Zajjaj said: this is specific to deception and disbelief, and he set the removal of harm against denial and disbelief. On this view, "min" in "minkum" is partitive (lil-tab'id), since the address is to people in general, and "the group" are the disbelievers. If the address is directed at the disbelievers, then "min" is explicative (lil-bayan).

The "lam" in ﴿that they may deny what We have given them﴾ is the lam of purpose (lam kay), that is: in order that they may deny what We have given them of the blessing of the removal of harm. So it is as though this denial on their part, which takes the place of the thanks that is obligatory upon them, is an aim and a goal among their aims. This is the extreme of obstinacy and stubbornness, beyond which there is nothing. It has been said that the lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), meaning that the outcome of those supplications was nothing but this disbelief.

Then He, glory be to Him, said, by way of threat and intimidation, shifting from the third person to the second person (iltifat): ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ So enjoy what you have of that. ﴿You will soon know﴾ the outcome of your affair, what will befall you in this world, and what you will come to in the Hereafter.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, related another type of their ugly deeds, saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share of what We have provided them.﴾ That is: this assigning occurs from them after they had cried out to Allah, glory be to Him, for the removal of harm from them, and after the disbelief and association with Him that follow the removal of harm. Yet despite this, they assign to what they do not know the reality of, namely inanimate objects and devils, a share of what We have provided them from their wealth, drawing near to them thereby.

It has also been said that the meaning is: they, that is the disbelievers, assign to the idols, while they know nothing because they are inanimate. On this view, the subject of "ya'lamun" (they know) is the idols, and they are treated as rational beings in their plural formation with the (masculine) plural suffix, in accordance with the disbelievers' belief concerning them.

The essential meaning is: these disbelievers assign to the idols, which do not understand anything, a share of their wealth which Allah has given them. ﴿By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.﴾ This is a return from the third person to the second person, and this questioning is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿About what you used to fabricate﴾ means what you invented of lies against Allah, glory be to Him, in this world.

﴿And they assign to Allah daughters.﴾ This is another kind of their scandals and ugly deeds. Khuza'ah and Kinanah used to say that the angels are the daughters of Allah, glory be to Him. He, glory be to Him, has exalted Himself above what these brutes attributed to Him, those who have no sound minds and no upright understanding: ﴿They are no more than cattle; rather, they are even more astray﴾ (al-Furqan 44). In this declaration of transcendence there is an expression of wonder at their condition. ﴿And for themselves is what they desire.﴾ That is: they assign to themselves what they desire of sons. The word "ma" is in the accusative position, governed by an implied verb, and it may also be in the nominative position as a subject (mubtada').

Al-Zajjaj rejected the accusative reading, saying: the Arabs do not say "ja'ala lahu kadha" (he made for him such-and-such) while meaning himself; rather they say "ja'ala li-nafsihi kadha" (he made for himself such-and-such). So if it were accusative, it would say "wa li-anfusihim ma yashtahun" (and for themselves what they desire).

But al-Farra' permitted the accusative reading.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned their aversion to the females whom they had assigned to Allah, saying: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female,﴾ that is, when one of them is informed of the birth of a daughter to him, ﴿his face becomes darkened,﴾ that is, changed. The intended meaning is not the blackness which is the opposite of whiteness, but rather a figurative use (kinayah) of blackness for dejection and change caused by the grief that results. The Arabs say of everyone who meets with something disagreeable: "his face has turned black with grief and sorrow." So said al-Zajjaj.

But al-Mawardi said: rather, the intended meaning is blackness of color in reality. He said: this is the view of the majority. The first view is more preferable, for it is known by experience that whoever becomes angry, grieved, or distressed does not have in his color anything but mere change and the appearance of gloominess and dejection, not real blackness. And the clause ﴿while he is suppressing [his rage].﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) (p-787), that is: full of grief, with suppressed anger and fury.

Al-Akhfash said: he is the one who suppresses his anger and does not show it. It has also been said that he is the one overcome with grief, whose mouth is closed from sorrow, derived from "al-kizamah," which is the sealing of the mouth of a well. This was said by Ali ibn Isa, and it has already been mentioned in Surah Yusuf.

﴿He hides himself from the people﴾ that is, he absconds and conceals himself, ﴿because of the ill of what he has been informed of.﴾ That is: because of the ill of grief, shame, and disgrace that befalls him by reason of the birth of a girl to him. ﴿Shall he keep it despite humiliation?﴾ That is: he remains continually wavering between two matters: either keeping the daughter he was informed of, or burying her in the dust, ﴿despite humiliation,﴾ that is, disgrace. So also did Isa al-Thaqafi read.

Al-Yazidi said: "al-hun" means humiliation in the dialect of Quraysh. So also did Abu Ubayd relate it from al-Kisa'i. And it is related from al-Kisa'i that it means affliction and hardship. Al-Khansa' said:

We humble souls, and the humbling of souls on the day of the terrible battle keeps them preserved.

Al-Farra' said: "al-hun" means "little" in the dialect of Tamim.

Al-Nahhas related from al-A'mash that he read: "Shall he keep it in disgrace, or bury it in the dust?" That is, hide it in the dust by burying it alive, as the Arabs used to do. So the one who has been informed of the birth of a female remains wavering between these two matters. The masculine pronoun in "yumsikuhu" and "yadussuhu" is used, despite its referring to the female, in observance of the wording.

Al-Jahdari read: "Or bury her in the dust." It would necessarily follow that he reads "Shall he keep her" (yumsikuha). It has also been said that "dass" (burying) means concealing her from people, so that she is not recognized, like something hidden because it is concealed from sight.

﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge.﴾ For they attributed the daughters, whom they dislike, to Allah, glory be to Him, and they attributed the sons, whom they love, to themselves. A similar statement is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That would be an unjust division﴾ (al-Najm 21–22).

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the attribute of evil.﴾ That is: for those whom Allah, glory be to Him, has described with these monstrous ugly qualities, is the attribute of evil, that is, the quality of evil, consisting of ignorance and disbelief in Allah. It has also been said that it is their description of Allah, glory be to Him, with a consort and a child. It has also been said that it is their need for a son to take their place, and the burying of daughters to avert shame and fear of poverty. It has also been said that it is punishment and the Fire. ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest attribute.﴾ That is the opposite of the attributes of created beings: complete wealth, all-encompassing generosity, and vast knowledge. Or it is oneness and sincerity in worship. Or it is that He is the Creator, the Provider, the Powerful, the Requiter. It has also been said that it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. And it has been said: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the parable of His light﴾ (al-Nur 35). ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, whom none can overpower, so their attributing to Him what is not befitting Him does Him no harm. ﴿The Wise﴾ in His acts and His sayings.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on surah 16, verses 51–68 (part 2 of 2):

Then, after Allah, glorified is He, related the great extent of the people's disbelief, He explained the breadth of His generosity and forbearance, in that He did not hasten to punish them and did not seize them for their wrongdoing. So He said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing﴾. By "the people" here is meant the disbelievers, or all the sinners. ﴿He would not leave upon it﴾, meaning upon the earth, even though it is not mentioned, for it is indicated by the mention of "the people" and the mention of "the creature" (*dābbah*). All of them are settled upon the earth. By "the creature" is meant the disbeliever, and it was said that it means everything that crawls. It has been asked, on this view: how can destruction encompass all of them when some of them have no sin? It is answered: the wrongdoer is destroyed as retribution against him, and the destruction of others, if they are among those who bear obligation, is for the sake of increasing their reward; and if they are from among others, then it is due to the evil consequence of the wrongdoing of the wrongdoers. And to Allah belongs the perfect wisdom. ﴿He is not asked about what He does, but they will be asked﴾ [al-Anbiya': 23]. A similar statement is His saying: ﴿And fear a trial which will not strike exclusively those of you who have done wrong﴾ [al-Anfal: 25].

Among the ḥadīths with this meaning is what is in Muslim and others, from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah intends a punishment for a people, the punishment strikes whoever is among them; then they will be raised according to their intentions." Likewise is the ḥadīth of the army that will be swallowed up in the desert, and at its end: that they will be raised according to their intentions. We have already presented, in the commentary on His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And fear a trial﴾ [al-Anfal: 25], and the verse, a genuine verification deserving of reference to it.

﴿But He delays them until a specified term﴾, known to Him, which is the end of their lives and the expiry of their lifespans, or the term of their punishment. In this delay there is profound wisdom, among which is establishing the proof against them (*al-iʿdhār*) and giving them latitude (*irkhāʾ al-ʿinān maʿahum*), and among which is the coming into being of those whom He foreknew from their offspring. ﴿So when their term comes﴾, which He has appointed for them, the word of Allah, glorified is He, will be fulfilled against them at that time, without advancing beyond it or delaying from it. The *sāʿah* is a short period of time, and its explanation and verification have already been presented.

Then He mentioned another type of their ignorance and foolishness, so He said: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾, meaning they ascribe to Him, glorified is He, what they dislike to be ascribed to themselves, namely daughters. This is a repetition of what has already been mentioned, for the purpose of emphasis and confirmation, and to increase the rebuke and reproach. ﴿And their tongues describe the lie﴾. This is from the other type which He, glorified is He, mentioned of their ugly deeds, and it is: that is, what their tongues describe of falsehood is their saying: ﴿that for them is the best﴾, i.e., the best attribute or the best outcome.

Al-Zajjaj said: they claim that they have, along with the ugliness of their statement, the good reward from Allah.

Al-Zajjaj also said, and al-Farrāʾ: ﴿that for them is the best﴾ is in apposition to ﴿their tongues describe the lie﴾, and *al-kadhib* (the lie) is in the accusative as the object of *taṣif* (describe).

Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, Mujāhid, and Ibn Muḥaysin read *al-kudhub* (with the *kāf*, *dhāl*, and *bāʾ* all vowelled with *ḍamma*), as an adjective to *al-alsun* (the tongues), and it is the plural of *kadhib*. In that case, the object according to this reading is ﴿that for them is the best﴾.

Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted them with His saying: ﴿Without doubt, for them is the Fire﴾, i.e., truly, for them, in place of what they assigned to themselves of the best, is the Fire. The verification of this has already been presented. ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾. Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Abū ʿUbaydah said: meaning, left behind and forgotten in the Fire. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ also said this, and so it is derived from "I *afraṭtu* so-and-so behind me," when I left him behind and forgot him.

Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: hastened toward it, sent forward into entering it, from "I *afraṭtuhu*," meaning I sent him ahead in seeking water. The *fāriṭ* is the one who goes ahead to the water, and the *furrāṭ* are those who go ahead in seeking water, and the *wurrād* are those who come later. From this is His saying (ﷺ): "I am your *faraṭ* at the Pool," meaning your one who goes ahead.

Al-Quṭāmī said:
*fa-staʿjalūnā wa-kānū min ṣaḥābatinā*
*kamā taʿajjala furrāṭun li-wurrādi*

Nāfiʿ, in the narration of Warsh, read *mufriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling (*wa-takhfīfihā*). This is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, and its meaning is: those who are extravagant in sins and disobediences. It is said: "So-and-so *afraṭa* over so-and-so" when he exceeded him and said to him more of the evil than he had said.

Abū Jaʿfar al-Qārī read *mufarriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and doubling it, meaning: those who neglect the command of Allah, so it is from *tafrīṭ* (neglect) regarding what is obligatory.

The rest read *mufraṭūn* with a *fatḥa* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling, and its meaning is: those sent ahead to the Fire.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid, regarding His saying: ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "The religion" is sincerity (*al-ikhlāṣ*), and *wāṣiban* means perpetual.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Abū Ṣāliḥ, regarding ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "There is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding *wāṣiban*: "perpetual."

Al-Firyābī and Ibn Jarīr transmitted from him: "obligatory."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿you cry out﴾: "you humbly supplicate with supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī: "you cry out in supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan regarding His saying: ﴿So enjoy, for you will soon know﴾: "It is a threat."

Ibn Jarīr transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know﴾, the verse: "They know that Allah created them, harms them and benefits them, and then they assign to what they do not know that it harms them and does not benefit them" ﴿a portion of what We have provided for them﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse: "They are the polytheists of the Arabs, who assigned to their idols and their devils a portion of what Allah had provided them, and set aside a part of their wealth, making it for their idols and their devils."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding the verse: "It is their saying: 'This is for Allah, according to their claim, and this is for our partners.'"

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to Allah daughters﴾, the verse: He says: "They assign to Me daughters, which they approve for Me but do not approve for themselves. That is because in the Jāhiliyyah, when a daughter was born to one of them, he kept her in humiliation, or buried her alive in the dust."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿And for them is what they desire﴾, he said: "It refers to sons."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Or does he bury it in the dust﴾, he said: "He buries his daughter alive."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge﴾, he said: "Evil is what they judged. He says: a thing they do not approve for themselves, so how would they approve it for Me?"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "It is the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "He says: there is nothing like Him."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿He has not left upon it any creature﴾, he said: "(i.e., He did not) give them rain."

He also transmitted from al-Suddī something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse, he said: "This was done in the time of Noah. Allah destroyed everything upon the surface of the earth of creatures, except what was carried in His ark."

Aḥmad in *al-Zuhd* transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "The sins of the son of Adam killed the dung beetle in its hole." Then he said: "By Allah, (this was) at the time of the drowning of the people of Noah."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from him: "The dung beetle was almost punished in its hole for the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted something similar from Anas.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, Ibn Jarīr, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from Abū Hurayrah that he heard a man say: "Indeed, the wrongdoer harms only himself." Abū Hurayrah said: "Yes, by Allah, indeed the bustard dies of emaciation in its nest because of the oppression of the oppressor."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk regarding ﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike﴾, he said: "They assign to Me daughters, and they dislike that for themselves."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best﴾, he said: "The statement of the disbelievers of Quraysh to us: 'For us are the sons, and for Him are the daughters.'"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah something similar.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾, he said: "Forgotten."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah, who said: "Hastened."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 16, verses 51–68 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glory be to Him, made clear that His created beings, both celestial and terrestrial, are subject to Him and humbled before His majesty, He followed this with a prohibition of association (shirk) in His words: ﴿And Allah said, "Do not take two gods. He is but one God."﴾ So He forbade taking two gods, then affirmed that divinity (al-ilahiyyah) is confined to one God, who is Allah, glory be to Him. It has been said that the dual form in "two gods" (ilahayn) indicates duality, and the singular in "God" (ilah) indicates unity. So what is the reason for describing "two gods" with "two" (ithnayn), and describing "God" with "one" (wahid)? The answer given is that there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir, rearrangement of words) in the speech, and the sense is: "Do not take two gods; He is only one God." It has also been said that the repetition is for the sake of emphasis in warning against taking a partner. It has also been said that the benefit of adding "two" is to make known that the prohibition concerns plurality and not the kind, and the benefit of adding "one" is to repel the supposition that the intent is only to affirm divinity without oneness, even though divinity itself is conceded to Him, glory be to Him, and the disagreement of the polytheists concerns only His oneness.

Then, by way of iltifat (shift from third person to first person), He, glory be to Him, moved the speech from the third person to the first person in order to increase the intimidation, saying: ﴿So it is Me that you should fear.﴾ That is: if you fear anything, then fear Me alone, not anyone else. The like of this has already passed at the beginning of al-Baqarah.

Then, when He had established His oneness, and that He is the One who must be singled out with fear and with hope directed to Him, He mentioned that all things are in His possession and under His disposal, saying: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This sentence confirms what came earlier in His words: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ (al-Nahl 49), to its end. The placing of the predicate first (taqdim al-khabar) serves to indicate exclusivity. ﴿And for Him is religion, constant.﴾ That is: established, obligatory, perpetual, not ceasing. Religion here means obedience and sincerity. Al-Farra' said: "wasiban" means "perpetual." From this is the verse of Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali:

I do not seek praise whose endurance is brief,
at the price of blame that lasts the whole age, perpetual.

That is: perpetual.

It is also narrated from al-Farra' that he said: "al-wasib" means "the sincere." But the first (meaning) is preferable. From this is His statement: ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾ (al-Saffat 9), that is, lasting.

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, obedience to Him is obligatory forever. Thus he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the obligatory."

Ibn Qutaybah said, in interpreting "al-wasib": no one is obeyed except that this (obedience) ceases through departure or destruction, except Allah, the Exalted, for obedience to Him endures. So he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the enduring." When a thing endures without ceasing, it becomes binding and established. It is said: "wasaba al-shay'u yasibu wusuban, fahuwa wasib," meaning it lasted; and "wasaba al-rajulu 'ala al-amr," meaning he persisted in it. It has also been said that "al-wasab" is fatigue and weariness, meaning that obedience to Allah, glory be to Him, is obligatory even if the servant becomes weary in it. But this does not suit what is in the verse.

The interrogative in His words: ﴿Then is it other than Allah you fear?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, and it is coordinated with an implied element, as in its counterparts. The meaning is: since religion, that is obedience, is obligatory for Him permanently without ceasing, it is fitting to restrict piety (taqwa) to Him and not to direct it to anyone else.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, bestowed favor upon them by stating that all the blessings in which they live come from Him and not from anyone else. He said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah.﴾ That is: whatever blessings come upon you, of their various kinds, are from Allah, that is, they are from Him. Thus "ma" may be conditional (shartiyyah), and it may also be relative (mawsulah) with the sense of a condition, with "bikum" as its complement. "Min ni'mah" is either a circumstantial element (hal) from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase, or an explanation (bayan) of "ma." His words ﴿then from Allah﴾ are the predicate. If "ma" is conditional, the verb of the condition is elided, that is, "ma yakun" (whatever may be). Blessing is either religious, which is knowledge of the truth for its own sake and knowledge of the good for the sake of acting upon it; or worldly, which is either psychological, physical or external, such as material prosperity and other things. Each of these is a genus under which there are countless kinds, and all of them are from Allah, glory be to Him. So the intelligent person should give thanks to none but Him.

Then He explained the fickleness of the human being after he is immersed in the sea of blessings, saying: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help.﴾ That is: when harm touches you, of any kind, you turn to Allah, glory be to Him, and not to anyone else, humbly seeking its removal, for there is no remover of it but Him. It is said: "ja'ara yaj'aru" in the language of the Arabs, "ju'aran," meaning he raised his voice in humble supplication.

Al-A'sha said, describing a cow:

She circled three times between day and night,
and the reproach was that she should circle and cry out.

Harm (al-durr) means illness, affliction, need, drought, and everything by which a person is harmed.

﴿Then when He removes the harm from you, behold, a group of you associate others with their Lord.﴾ That is: when He removes from you the harm that had befallen you, behold, a group among you, those whose harm has been removed, associate others with their Lord, placing with Him another god, such as an idol or the like. The verse is brought to express wonder at the conduct of these people, who place partnership with Allah, who bestowed favor upon them by removing the harm that had befallen them, in place of gratitude to Him. This meaning has already appeared in al-An'am and Yunus, and will come in al-Isra'.

Al-Zajjaj said: this is specific to deception and disbelief, and he set the removal of harm against denial and disbelief. On this view, "min" in "minkum" is partitive (lil-tab'id), since the address is to people in general, and "the group" are the disbelievers. If the address is directed at the disbelievers, then "min" is explicative (lil-bayan).

The "lam" in ﴿that they may deny what We have given them﴾ is the lam of purpose (lam kay), that is: in order that they may deny what We have given them of the blessing of the removal of harm. So it is as though this denial on their part, which takes the place of the thanks that is obligatory upon them, is an aim and a goal among their aims. This is the extreme of obstinacy and stubbornness, beyond which there is nothing. It has been said that the lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), meaning that the outcome of those supplications was nothing but this disbelief.

Then He, glory be to Him, said, by way of threat and intimidation, shifting from the third person to the second person (iltifat): ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ So enjoy what you have of that. ﴿You will soon know﴾ the outcome of your affair, what will befall you in this world, and what you will come to in the Hereafter.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, related another type of their ugly deeds, saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share of what We have provided them.﴾ That is: this assigning occurs from them after they had cried out to Allah, glory be to Him, for the removal of harm from them, and after the disbelief and association with Him that follow the removal of harm. Yet despite this, they assign to what they do not know the reality of, namely inanimate objects and devils, a share of what We have provided them from their wealth, drawing near to them thereby.

It has also been said that the meaning is: they, that is the disbelievers, assign to the idols, while they know nothing because they are inanimate. On this view, the subject of "ya'lamun" (they know) is the idols, and they are treated as rational beings in their plural formation with the (masculine) plural suffix, in accordance with the disbelievers' belief concerning them.

The essential meaning is: these disbelievers assign to the idols, which do not understand anything, a share of their wealth which Allah has given them. ﴿By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.﴾ This is a return from the third person to the second person, and this questioning is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿About what you used to fabricate﴾ means what you invented of lies against Allah, glory be to Him, in this world.

﴿And they assign to Allah daughters.﴾ This is another kind of their scandals and ugly deeds. Khuza'ah and Kinanah used to say that the angels are the daughters of Allah, glory be to Him. He, glory be to Him, has exalted Himself above what these brutes attributed to Him, those who have no sound minds and no upright understanding: ﴿They are no more than cattle; rather, they are even more astray﴾ (al-Furqan 44). In this declaration of transcendence there is an expression of wonder at their condition. ﴿And for themselves is what they desire.﴾ That is: they assign to themselves what they desire of sons. The word "ma" is in the accusative position, governed by an implied verb, and it may also be in the nominative position as a subject (mubtada').

Al-Zajjaj rejected the accusative reading, saying: the Arabs do not say "ja'ala lahu kadha" (he made for him such-and-such) while meaning himself; rather they say "ja'ala li-nafsihi kadha" (he made for himself such-and-such). So if it were accusative, it would say "wa li-anfusihim ma yashtahun" (and for themselves what they desire).

But al-Farra' permitted the accusative reading.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned their aversion to the females whom they had assigned to Allah, saying: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female,﴾ that is, when one of them is informed of the birth of a daughter to him, ﴿his face becomes darkened,﴾ that is, changed. The intended meaning is not the blackness which is the opposite of whiteness, but rather a figurative use (kinayah) of blackness for dejection and change caused by the grief that results. The Arabs say of everyone who meets with something disagreeable: "his face has turned black with grief and sorrow." So said al-Zajjaj.

But al-Mawardi said: rather, the intended meaning is blackness of color in reality. He said: this is the view of the majority. The first view is more preferable, for it is known by experience that whoever becomes angry, grieved, or distressed does not have in his color anything but mere change and the appearance of gloominess and dejection, not real blackness. And the clause ﴿while he is suppressing [his rage].﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) (p-787), that is: full of grief, with suppressed anger and fury.

Al-Akhfash said: he is the one who suppresses his anger and does not show it. It has also been said that he is the one overcome with grief, whose mouth is closed from sorrow, derived from "al-kizamah," which is the sealing of the mouth of a well. This was said by Ali ibn Isa, and it has already been mentioned in Surah Yusuf.

﴿He hides himself from the people﴾ that is, he absconds and conceals himself, ﴿because of the ill of what he has been informed of.﴾ That is: because of the ill of grief, shame, and disgrace that befalls him by reason of the birth of a girl to him. ﴿Shall he keep it despite humiliation?﴾ That is: he remains continually wavering between two matters: either keeping the daughter he was informed of, or burying her in the dust, ﴿despite humiliation,﴾ that is, disgrace. So also did Isa al-Thaqafi read.

Al-Yazidi said: "al-hun" means humiliation in the dialect of Quraysh. So also did Abu Ubayd relate it from al-Kisa'i. And it is related from al-Kisa'i that it means affliction and hardship. Al-Khansa' said:

We humble souls, and the humbling of souls on the day of the terrible battle keeps them preserved.

Al-Farra' said: "al-hun" means "little" in the dialect of Tamim.

Al-Nahhas related from al-A'mash that he read: "Shall he keep it in disgrace, or bury it in the dust?" That is, hide it in the dust by burying it alive, as the Arabs used to do. So the one who has been informed of the birth of a female remains wavering between these two matters. The masculine pronoun in "yumsikuhu" and "yadussuhu" is used, despite its referring to the female, in observance of the wording.

Al-Jahdari read: "Or bury her in the dust." It would necessarily follow that he reads "Shall he keep her" (yumsikuha). It has also been said that "dass" (burying) means concealing her from people, so that she is not recognized, like something hidden because it is concealed from sight.

﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge.﴾ For they attributed the daughters, whom they dislike, to Allah, glory be to Him, and they attributed the sons, whom they love, to themselves. A similar statement is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That would be an unjust division﴾ (al-Najm 21–22).

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the attribute of evil.﴾ That is: for those whom Allah, glory be to Him, has described with these monstrous ugly qualities, is the attribute of evil, that is, the quality of evil, consisting of ignorance and disbelief in Allah. It has also been said that it is their description of Allah, glory be to Him, with a consort and a child. It has also been said that it is their need for a son to take their place, and the burying of daughters to avert shame and fear of poverty. It has also been said that it is punishment and the Fire. ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest attribute.﴾ That is the opposite of the attributes of created beings: complete wealth, all-encompassing generosity, and vast knowledge. Or it is oneness and sincerity in worship. Or it is that He is the Creator, the Provider, the Powerful, the Requiter. It has also been said that it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. And it has been said: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the parable of His light﴾ (al-Nur 35). ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, whom none can overpower, so their attributing to Him what is not befitting Him does Him no harm. ﴿The Wise﴾ in His acts and His sayings.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on surah 16, verses 51–68 (part 2 of 2):

Then, after Allah, glorified is He, related the great extent of the people's disbelief, He explained the breadth of His generosity and forbearance, in that He did not hasten to punish them and did not seize them for their wrongdoing. So He said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing﴾. By "the people" here is meant the disbelievers, or all the sinners. ﴿He would not leave upon it﴾, meaning upon the earth, even though it is not mentioned, for it is indicated by the mention of "the people" and the mention of "the creature" (*dābbah*). All of them are settled upon the earth. By "the creature" is meant the disbeliever, and it was said that it means everything that crawls. It has been asked, on this view: how can destruction encompass all of them when some of them have no sin? It is answered: the wrongdoer is destroyed as retribution against him, and the destruction of others, if they are among those who bear obligation, is for the sake of increasing their reward; and if they are from among others, then it is due to the evil consequence of the wrongdoing of the wrongdoers. And to Allah belongs the perfect wisdom. ﴿He is not asked about what He does, but they will be asked﴾ [al-Anbiya': 23]. A similar statement is His saying: ﴿And fear a trial which will not strike exclusively those of you who have done wrong﴾ [al-Anfal: 25].

Among the ḥadīths with this meaning is what is in Muslim and others, from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah intends a punishment for a people, the punishment strikes whoever is among them; then they will be raised according to their intentions." Likewise is the ḥadīth of the army that will be swallowed up in the desert, and at its end: that they will be raised according to their intentions. We have already presented, in the commentary on His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And fear a trial﴾ [al-Anfal: 25], and the verse, a genuine verification deserving of reference to it.

﴿But He delays them until a specified term﴾, known to Him, which is the end of their lives and the expiry of their lifespans, or the term of their punishment. In this delay there is profound wisdom, among which is establishing the proof against them (*al-iʿdhār*) and giving them latitude (*irkhāʾ al-ʿinān maʿahum*), and among which is the coming into being of those whom He foreknew from their offspring. ﴿So when their term comes﴾, which He has appointed for them, the word of Allah, glorified is He, will be fulfilled against them at that time, without advancing beyond it or delaying from it. The *sāʿah* is a short period of time, and its explanation and verification have already been presented.

Then He mentioned another type of their ignorance and foolishness, so He said: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾, meaning they ascribe to Him, glorified is He, what they dislike to be ascribed to themselves, namely daughters. This is a repetition of what has already been mentioned, for the purpose of emphasis and confirmation, and to increase the rebuke and reproach. ﴿And their tongues describe the lie﴾. This is from the other type which He, glorified is He, mentioned of their ugly deeds, and it is: that is, what their tongues describe of falsehood is their saying: ﴿that for them is the best﴾, i.e., the best attribute or the best outcome.

Al-Zajjaj said: they claim that they have, along with the ugliness of their statement, the good reward from Allah.

Al-Zajjaj also said, and al-Farrāʾ: ﴿that for them is the best﴾ is in apposition to ﴿their tongues describe the lie﴾, and *al-kadhib* (the lie) is in the accusative as the object of *taṣif* (describe).

Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, Mujāhid, and Ibn Muḥaysin read *al-kudhub* (with the *kāf*, *dhāl*, and *bāʾ* all vowelled with *ḍamma*), as an adjective to *al-alsun* (the tongues), and it is the plural of *kadhib*. In that case, the object according to this reading is ﴿that for them is the best﴾.

Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted them with His saying: ﴿Without doubt, for them is the Fire﴾, i.e., truly, for them, in place of what they assigned to themselves of the best, is the Fire. The verification of this has already been presented. ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾. Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Abū ʿUbaydah said: meaning, left behind and forgotten in the Fire. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ also said this, and so it is derived from "I *afraṭtu* so-and-so behind me," when I left him behind and forgot him.

Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: hastened toward it, sent forward into entering it, from "I *afraṭtuhu*," meaning I sent him ahead in seeking water. The *fāriṭ* is the one who goes ahead to the water, and the *furrāṭ* are those who go ahead in seeking water, and the *wurrād* are those who come later. From this is His saying (ﷺ): "I am your *faraṭ* at the Pool," meaning your one who goes ahead.

Al-Quṭāmī said:
*fa-staʿjalūnā wa-kānū min ṣaḥābatinā*
*kamā taʿajjala furrāṭun li-wurrādi*

Nāfiʿ, in the narration of Warsh, read *mufriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling (*wa-takhfīfihā*). This is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, and its meaning is: those who are extravagant in sins and disobediences. It is said: "So-and-so *afraṭa* over so-and-so" when he exceeded him and said to him more of the evil than he had said.

Abū Jaʿfar al-Qārī read *mufarriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and doubling it, meaning: those who neglect the command of Allah, so it is from *tafrīṭ* (neglect) regarding what is obligatory.

The rest read *mufraṭūn* with a *fatḥa* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling, and its meaning is: those sent ahead to the Fire.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid, regarding His saying: ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "The religion" is sincerity (*al-ikhlāṣ*), and *wāṣiban* means perpetual.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Abū Ṣāliḥ, regarding ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "There is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding *wāṣiban*: "perpetual."

Al-Firyābī and Ibn Jarīr transmitted from him: "obligatory."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿you cry out﴾: "you humbly supplicate with supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī: "you cry out in supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan regarding His saying: ﴿So enjoy, for you will soon know﴾: "It is a threat."

Ibn Jarīr transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know﴾, the verse: "They know that Allah created them, harms them and benefits them, and then they assign to what they do not know that it harms them and does not benefit them" ﴿a portion of what We have provided for them﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse: "They are the polytheists of the Arabs, who assigned to their idols and their devils a portion of what Allah had provided them, and set aside a part of their wealth, making it for their idols and their devils."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding the verse: "It is their saying: 'This is for Allah, according to their claim, and this is for our partners.'"

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to Allah daughters﴾, the verse: He says: "They assign to Me daughters, which they approve for Me but do not approve for themselves. That is because in the Jāhiliyyah, when a daughter was born to one of them, he kept her in humiliation, or buried her alive in the dust."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿And for them is what they desire﴾, he said: "It refers to sons."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Or does he bury it in the dust﴾, he said: "He buries his daughter alive."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge﴾, he said: "Evil is what they judged. He says: a thing they do not approve for themselves, so how would they approve it for Me?"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "It is the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "He says: there is nothing like Him."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿He has not left upon it any creature﴾, he said: "(i.e., He did not) give them rain."

He also transmitted from al-Suddī something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse, he said: "This was done in the time of Noah. Allah destroyed everything upon the surface of the earth of creatures, except what was carried in His ark."

Aḥmad in *al-Zuhd* transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "The sins of the son of Adam killed the dung beetle in its hole." Then he said: "By Allah, (this was) at the time of the drowning of the people of Noah."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from him: "The dung beetle was almost punished in its hole for the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted something similar from Anas.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, Ibn Jarīr, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from Abū Hurayrah that he heard a man say: "Indeed, the wrongdoer harms only himself." Abū Hurayrah said: "Yes, by Allah, indeed the bustard dies of emaciation in its nest because of the oppression of the oppressor."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk regarding ﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike﴾, he said: "They assign to Me daughters, and they dislike that for themselves."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best﴾, he said: "The statement of the disbelievers of Quraysh to us: 'For us are the sons, and for Him are the daughters.'"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah something similar.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾, he said: "Forgotten."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah, who said: "Hastened."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 16, verses 51–68 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glory be to Him, made clear that His created beings, both celestial and terrestrial, are subject to Him and humbled before His majesty, He followed this with a prohibition of association (shirk) in His words: ﴿And Allah said, "Do not take two gods. He is but one God."﴾ So He forbade taking two gods, then affirmed that divinity (al-ilahiyyah) is confined to one God, who is Allah, glory be to Him. It has been said that the dual form in "two gods" (ilahayn) indicates duality, and the singular in "God" (ilah) indicates unity. So what is the reason for describing "two gods" with "two" (ithnayn), and describing "God" with "one" (wahid)? The answer given is that there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir, rearrangement of words) in the speech, and the sense is: "Do not take two gods; He is only one God." It has also been said that the repetition is for the sake of emphasis in warning against taking a partner. It has also been said that the benefit of adding "two" is to make known that the prohibition concerns plurality and not the kind, and the benefit of adding "one" is to repel the supposition that the intent is only to affirm divinity without oneness, even though divinity itself is conceded to Him, glory be to Him, and the disagreement of the polytheists concerns only His oneness.

Then, by way of iltifat (shift from third person to first person), He, glory be to Him, moved the speech from the third person to the first person in order to increase the intimidation, saying: ﴿So it is Me that you should fear.﴾ That is: if you fear anything, then fear Me alone, not anyone else. The like of this has already passed at the beginning of al-Baqarah.

Then, when He had established His oneness, and that He is the One who must be singled out with fear and with hope directed to Him, He mentioned that all things are in His possession and under His disposal, saying: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This sentence confirms what came earlier in His words: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ (al-Nahl 49), to its end. The placing of the predicate first (taqdim al-khabar) serves to indicate exclusivity. ﴿And for Him is religion, constant.﴾ That is: established, obligatory, perpetual, not ceasing. Religion here means obedience and sincerity. Al-Farra' said: "wasiban" means "perpetual." From this is the verse of Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali:

I do not seek praise whose endurance is brief,
at the price of blame that lasts the whole age, perpetual.

That is: perpetual.

It is also narrated from al-Farra' that he said: "al-wasib" means "the sincere." But the first (meaning) is preferable. From this is His statement: ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾ (al-Saffat 9), that is, lasting.

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, obedience to Him is obligatory forever. Thus he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the obligatory."

Ibn Qutaybah said, in interpreting "al-wasib": no one is obeyed except that this (obedience) ceases through departure or destruction, except Allah, the Exalted, for obedience to Him endures. So he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the enduring." When a thing endures without ceasing, it becomes binding and established. It is said: "wasaba al-shay'u yasibu wusuban, fahuwa wasib," meaning it lasted; and "wasaba al-rajulu 'ala al-amr," meaning he persisted in it. It has also been said that "al-wasab" is fatigue and weariness, meaning that obedience to Allah, glory be to Him, is obligatory even if the servant becomes weary in it. But this does not suit what is in the verse.

The interrogative in His words: ﴿Then is it other than Allah you fear?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, and it is coordinated with an implied element, as in its counterparts. The meaning is: since religion, that is obedience, is obligatory for Him permanently without ceasing, it is fitting to restrict piety (taqwa) to Him and not to direct it to anyone else.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, bestowed favor upon them by stating that all the blessings in which they live come from Him and not from anyone else. He said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah.﴾ That is: whatever blessings come upon you, of their various kinds, are from Allah, that is, they are from Him. Thus "ma" may be conditional (shartiyyah), and it may also be relative (mawsulah) with the sense of a condition, with "bikum" as its complement. "Min ni'mah" is either a circumstantial element (hal) from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase, or an explanation (bayan) of "ma." His words ﴿then from Allah﴾ are the predicate. If "ma" is conditional, the verb of the condition is elided, that is, "ma yakun" (whatever may be). Blessing is either religious, which is knowledge of the truth for its own sake and knowledge of the good for the sake of acting upon it; or worldly, which is either psychological, physical or external, such as material prosperity and other things. Each of these is a genus under which there are countless kinds, and all of them are from Allah, glory be to Him. So the intelligent person should give thanks to none but Him.

Then He explained the fickleness of the human being after he is immersed in the sea of blessings, saying: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help.﴾ That is: when harm touches you, of any kind, you turn to Allah, glory be to Him, and not to anyone else, humbly seeking its removal, for there is no remover of it but Him. It is said: "ja'ara yaj'aru" in the language of the Arabs, "ju'aran," meaning he raised his voice in humble supplication.

Al-A'sha said, describing a cow:

She circled three times between day and night,
and the reproach was that she should circle and cry out.

Harm (al-durr) means illness, affliction, need, drought, and everything by which a person is harmed.

﴿Then when He removes the harm from you, behold, a group of you associate others with their Lord.﴾ That is: when He removes from you the harm that had befallen you, behold, a group among you, those whose harm has been removed, associate others with their Lord, placing with Him another god, such as an idol or the like. The verse is brought to express wonder at the conduct of these people, who place partnership with Allah, who bestowed favor upon them by removing the harm that had befallen them, in place of gratitude to Him. This meaning has already appeared in al-An'am and Yunus, and will come in al-Isra'.

Al-Zajjaj said: this is specific to deception and disbelief, and he set the removal of harm against denial and disbelief. On this view, "min" in "minkum" is partitive (lil-tab'id), since the address is to people in general, and "the group" are the disbelievers. If the address is directed at the disbelievers, then "min" is explicative (lil-bayan).

The "lam" in ﴿that they may deny what We have given them﴾ is the lam of purpose (lam kay), that is: in order that they may deny what We have given them of the blessing of the removal of harm. So it is as though this denial on their part, which takes the place of the thanks that is obligatory upon them, is an aim and a goal among their aims. This is the extreme of obstinacy and stubbornness, beyond which there is nothing. It has been said that the lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), meaning that the outcome of those supplications was nothing but this disbelief.

Then He, glory be to Him, said, by way of threat and intimidation, shifting from the third person to the second person (iltifat): ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ So enjoy what you have of that. ﴿You will soon know﴾ the outcome of your affair, what will befall you in this world, and what you will come to in the Hereafter.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, related another type of their ugly deeds, saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share of what We have provided them.﴾ That is: this assigning occurs from them after they had cried out to Allah, glory be to Him, for the removal of harm from them, and after the disbelief and association with Him that follow the removal of harm. Yet despite this, they assign to what they do not know the reality of, namely inanimate objects and devils, a share of what We have provided them from their wealth, drawing near to them thereby.

It has also been said that the meaning is: they, that is the disbelievers, assign to the idols, while they know nothing because they are inanimate. On this view, the subject of "ya'lamun" (they know) is the idols, and they are treated as rational beings in their plural formation with the (masculine) plural suffix, in accordance with the disbelievers' belief concerning them.

The essential meaning is: these disbelievers assign to the idols, which do not understand anything, a share of their wealth which Allah has given them. ﴿By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.﴾ This is a return from the third person to the second person, and this questioning is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿About what you used to fabricate﴾ means what you invented of lies against Allah, glory be to Him, in this world.

﴿And they assign to Allah daughters.﴾ This is another kind of their scandals and ugly deeds. Khuza'ah and Kinanah used to say that the angels are the daughters of Allah, glory be to Him. He, glory be to Him, has exalted Himself above what these brutes attributed to Him, those who have no sound minds and no upright understanding: ﴿They are no more than cattle; rather, they are even more astray﴾ (al-Furqan 44). In this declaration of transcendence there is an expression of wonder at their condition. ﴿And for themselves is what they desire.﴾ That is: they assign to themselves what they desire of sons. The word "ma" is in the accusative position, governed by an implied verb, and it may also be in the nominative position as a subject (mubtada').

Al-Zajjaj rejected the accusative reading, saying: the Arabs do not say "ja'ala lahu kadha" (he made for him such-and-such) while meaning himself; rather they say "ja'ala li-nafsihi kadha" (he made for himself such-and-such). So if it were accusative, it would say "wa li-anfusihim ma yashtahun" (and for themselves what they desire).

But al-Farra' permitted the accusative reading.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned their aversion to the females whom they had assigned to Allah, saying: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female,﴾ that is, when one of them is informed of the birth of a daughter to him, ﴿his face becomes darkened,﴾ that is, changed. The intended meaning is not the blackness which is the opposite of whiteness, but rather a figurative use (kinayah) of blackness for dejection and change caused by the grief that results. The Arabs say of everyone who meets with something disagreeable: "his face has turned black with grief and sorrow." So said al-Zajjaj.

But al-Mawardi said: rather, the intended meaning is blackness of color in reality. He said: this is the view of the majority. The first view is more preferable, for it is known by experience that whoever becomes angry, grieved, or distressed does not have in his color anything but mere change and the appearance of gloominess and dejection, not real blackness. And the clause ﴿while he is suppressing [his rage].﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) (p-787), that is: full of grief, with suppressed anger and fury.

Al-Akhfash said: he is the one who suppresses his anger and does not show it. It has also been said that he is the one overcome with grief, whose mouth is closed from sorrow, derived from "al-kizamah," which is the sealing of the mouth of a well. This was said by Ali ibn Isa, and it has already been mentioned in Surah Yusuf.

﴿He hides himself from the people﴾ that is, he absconds and conceals himself, ﴿because of the ill of what he has been informed of.﴾ That is: because of the ill of grief, shame, and disgrace that befalls him by reason of the birth of a girl to him. ﴿Shall he keep it despite humiliation?﴾ That is: he remains continually wavering between two matters: either keeping the daughter he was informed of, or burying her in the dust, ﴿despite humiliation,﴾ that is, disgrace. So also did Isa al-Thaqafi read.

Al-Yazidi said: "al-hun" means humiliation in the dialect of Quraysh. So also did Abu Ubayd relate it from al-Kisa'i. And it is related from al-Kisa'i that it means affliction and hardship. Al-Khansa' said:

We humble souls, and the humbling of souls on the day of the terrible battle keeps them preserved.

Al-Farra' said: "al-hun" means "little" in the dialect of Tamim.

Al-Nahhas related from al-A'mash that he read: "Shall he keep it in disgrace, or bury it in the dust?" That is, hide it in the dust by burying it alive, as the Arabs used to do. So the one who has been informed of the birth of a female remains wavering between these two matters. The masculine pronoun in "yumsikuhu" and "yadussuhu" is used, despite its referring to the female, in observance of the wording.

Al-Jahdari read: "Or bury her in the dust." It would necessarily follow that he reads "Shall he keep her" (yumsikuha). It has also been said that "dass" (burying) means concealing her from people, so that she is not recognized, like something hidden because it is concealed from sight.

﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge.﴾ For they attributed the daughters, whom they dislike, to Allah, glory be to Him, and they attributed the sons, whom they love, to themselves. A similar statement is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That would be an unjust division﴾ (al-Najm 21–22).

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the attribute of evil.﴾ That is: for those whom Allah, glory be to Him, has described with these monstrous ugly qualities, is the attribute of evil, that is, the quality of evil, consisting of ignorance and disbelief in Allah. It has also been said that it is their description of Allah, glory be to Him, with a consort and a child. It has also been said that it is their need for a son to take their place, and the burying of daughters to avert shame and fear of poverty. It has also been said that it is punishment and the Fire. ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest attribute.﴾ That is the opposite of the attributes of created beings: complete wealth, all-encompassing generosity, and vast knowledge. Or it is oneness and sincerity in worship. Or it is that He is the Creator, the Provider, the Powerful, the Requiter. It has also been said that it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. And it has been said: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the parable of His light﴾ (al-Nur 35). ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, whom none can overpower, so their attributing to Him what is not befitting Him does Him no harm. ﴿The Wise﴾ in His acts and His sayings.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on surah 16, verses 51–68 (part 2 of 2):

Then, after Allah, glorified is He, related the great extent of the people's disbelief, He explained the breadth of His generosity and forbearance, in that He did not hasten to punish them and did not seize them for their wrongdoing. So He said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing﴾. By "the people" here is meant the disbelievers, or all the sinners. ﴿He would not leave upon it﴾, meaning upon the earth, even though it is not mentioned, for it is indicated by the mention of "the people" and the mention of "the creature" (*dābbah*). All of them are settled upon the earth. By "the creature" is meant the disbeliever, and it was said that it means everything that crawls. It has been asked, on this view: how can destruction encompass all of them when some of them have no sin? It is answered: the wrongdoer is destroyed as retribution against him, and the destruction of others, if they are among those who bear obligation, is for the sake of increasing their reward; and if they are from among others, then it is due to the evil consequence of the wrongdoing of the wrongdoers. And to Allah belongs the perfect wisdom. ﴿He is not asked about what He does, but they will be asked﴾ [al-Anbiya': 23]. A similar statement is His saying: ﴿And fear a trial which will not strike exclusively those of you who have done wrong﴾ [al-Anfal: 25].

Among the ḥadīths with this meaning is what is in Muslim and others, from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah intends a punishment for a people, the punishment strikes whoever is among them; then they will be raised according to their intentions." Likewise is the ḥadīth of the army that will be swallowed up in the desert, and at its end: that they will be raised according to their intentions. We have already presented, in the commentary on His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And fear a trial﴾ [al-Anfal: 25], and the verse, a genuine verification deserving of reference to it.

﴿But He delays them until a specified term﴾, known to Him, which is the end of their lives and the expiry of their lifespans, or the term of their punishment. In this delay there is profound wisdom, among which is establishing the proof against them (*al-iʿdhār*) and giving them latitude (*irkhāʾ al-ʿinān maʿahum*), and among which is the coming into being of those whom He foreknew from their offspring. ﴿So when their term comes﴾, which He has appointed for them, the word of Allah, glorified is He, will be fulfilled against them at that time, without advancing beyond it or delaying from it. The *sāʿah* is a short period of time, and its explanation and verification have already been presented.

Then He mentioned another type of their ignorance and foolishness, so He said: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾, meaning they ascribe to Him, glorified is He, what they dislike to be ascribed to themselves, namely daughters. This is a repetition of what has already been mentioned, for the purpose of emphasis and confirmation, and to increase the rebuke and reproach. ﴿And their tongues describe the lie﴾. This is from the other type which He, glorified is He, mentioned of their ugly deeds, and it is: that is, what their tongues describe of falsehood is their saying: ﴿that for them is the best﴾, i.e., the best attribute or the best outcome.

Al-Zajjaj said: they claim that they have, along with the ugliness of their statement, the good reward from Allah.

Al-Zajjaj also said, and al-Farrāʾ: ﴿that for them is the best﴾ is in apposition to ﴿their tongues describe the lie﴾, and *al-kadhib* (the lie) is in the accusative as the object of *taṣif* (describe).

Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, Mujāhid, and Ibn Muḥaysin read *al-kudhub* (with the *kāf*, *dhāl*, and *bāʾ* all vowelled with *ḍamma*), as an adjective to *al-alsun* (the tongues), and it is the plural of *kadhib*. In that case, the object according to this reading is ﴿that for them is the best﴾.

Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted them with His saying: ﴿Without doubt, for them is the Fire﴾, i.e., truly, for them, in place of what they assigned to themselves of the best, is the Fire. The verification of this has already been presented. ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾. Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Abū ʿUbaydah said: meaning, left behind and forgotten in the Fire. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ also said this, and so it is derived from "I *afraṭtu* so-and-so behind me," when I left him behind and forgot him.

Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: hastened toward it, sent forward into entering it, from "I *afraṭtuhu*," meaning I sent him ahead in seeking water. The *fāriṭ* is the one who goes ahead to the water, and the *furrāṭ* are those who go ahead in seeking water, and the *wurrād* are those who come later. From this is His saying (ﷺ): "I am your *faraṭ* at the Pool," meaning your one who goes ahead.

Al-Quṭāmī said:
*fa-staʿjalūnā wa-kānū min ṣaḥābatinā*
*kamā taʿajjala furrāṭun li-wurrādi*

Nāfiʿ, in the narration of Warsh, read *mufriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling (*wa-takhfīfihā*). This is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, and its meaning is: those who are extravagant in sins and disobediences. It is said: "So-and-so *afraṭa* over so-and-so" when he exceeded him and said to him more of the evil than he had said.

Abū Jaʿfar al-Qārī read *mufarriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and doubling it, meaning: those who neglect the command of Allah, so it is from *tafrīṭ* (neglect) regarding what is obligatory.

The rest read *mufraṭūn* with a *fatḥa* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling, and its meaning is: those sent ahead to the Fire.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid, regarding His saying: ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "The religion" is sincerity (*al-ikhlāṣ*), and *wāṣiban* means perpetual.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Abū Ṣāliḥ, regarding ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "There is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding *wāṣiban*: "perpetual."

Al-Firyābī and Ibn Jarīr transmitted from him: "obligatory."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿you cry out﴾: "you humbly supplicate with supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī: "you cry out in supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan regarding His saying: ﴿So enjoy, for you will soon know﴾: "It is a threat."

Ibn Jarīr transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know﴾, the verse: "They know that Allah created them, harms them and benefits them, and then they assign to what they do not know that it harms them and does not benefit them" ﴿a portion of what We have provided for them﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse: "They are the polytheists of the Arabs, who assigned to their idols and their devils a portion of what Allah had provided them, and set aside a part of their wealth, making it for their idols and their devils."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding the verse: "It is their saying: 'This is for Allah, according to their claim, and this is for our partners.'"

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to Allah daughters﴾, the verse: He says: "They assign to Me daughters, which they approve for Me but do not approve for themselves. That is because in the Jāhiliyyah, when a daughter was born to one of them, he kept her in humiliation, or buried her alive in the dust."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿And for them is what they desire﴾, he said: "It refers to sons."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Or does he bury it in the dust﴾, he said: "He buries his daughter alive."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge﴾, he said: "Evil is what they judged. He says: a thing they do not approve for themselves, so how would they approve it for Me?"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "It is the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "He says: there is nothing like Him."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿He has not left upon it any creature﴾, he said: "(i.e., He did not) give them rain."

He also transmitted from al-Suddī something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse, he said: "This was done in the time of Noah. Allah destroyed everything upon the surface of the earth of creatures, except what was carried in His ark."

Aḥmad in *al-Zuhd* transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "The sins of the son of Adam killed the dung beetle in its hole." Then he said: "By Allah, (this was) at the time of the drowning of the people of Noah."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from him: "The dung beetle was almost punished in its hole for the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted something similar from Anas.
