It is also narrated from al-Farra' that he said: "al-wasib" means "the sincere." But the first (meaning) is preferable. From this is His statement: ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾ (al-Saffat 9), that is, lasting.

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, obedience to Him is obligatory forever. Thus he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the obligatory."

Ibn Qutaybah said, in interpreting "al-wasib": no one is obeyed except that this (obedience) ceases through departure or destruction, except Allah, the Exalted, for obedience to Him endures. So he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the enduring." When a thing endures without ceasing, it becomes binding and established. It is said: "wasaba al-shay'u yasibu wusuban, fahuwa wasib," meaning it lasted; and "wasaba al-rajulu 'ala al-amr," meaning he persisted in it. It has also been said that "al-wasab" is fatigue and weariness, meaning that obedience to Allah, glory be to Him, is obligatory even if the servant becomes weary in it. But this does not suit what is in the verse.

The interrogative in His words: ﴿Then is it other than Allah you fear?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, and it is coordinated with an implied element, as in its counterparts. The meaning is: since religion, that is obedience, is obligatory for Him permanently without ceasing, it is fitting to restrict piety (taqwa) to Him and not to direct it to anyone else.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, bestowed favor upon them by stating that all the blessings in which they live come from Him and not from anyone else. He said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah.﴾ That is: whatever blessings come upon you, of their various kinds, are from Allah, that is, they are from Him. Thus "ma" may be conditional (shartiyyah), and it may also be relative (mawsulah) with the sense of a condition, with "bikum" as its complement. "Min ni'mah" is either a circumstantial element (hal) from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase, or an explanation (bayan) of "ma." His words ﴿then from Allah﴾ are the predicate. If "ma" is conditional, the verb of the condition is elided, that is, "ma yakun" (whatever may be). Blessing is either religious, which is knowledge of the truth for its own sake and knowledge of the good for the sake of acting upon it; or worldly, which is either psychological, physical or external, such as material prosperity and other things. Each of these is a genus under which there are countless kinds, and all of them are from Allah, glory be to Him. So the intelligent person should give thanks to none but Him.

Then He explained the fickleness of the human being after he is immersed in the sea of blessings, saying: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help.﴾ That is: when harm touches you, of any kind, you turn to Allah, glory be to Him, and not to anyone else, humbly seeking its removal, for there is no remover of it but Him. It is said: "ja'ara yaj'aru" in the language of the Arabs, "ju'aran," meaning he raised his voice in humble supplication.

Al-A'sha said, describing a cow:

She circled three times between day and night,
and the reproach was that she should circle and cry out.

Harm (al-durr) means illness, affliction, need, drought, and everything by which a person is harmed.

﴿Then when He removes the harm from you, behold, a group of you associate others with their Lord.﴾ That is: when He removes from you the harm that had befallen you, behold, a group among you, those whose harm has been removed, associate others with their Lord, placing with Him another god, such as an idol or the like. The verse is brought to express wonder at the conduct of these people, who place partnership with Allah, who bestowed favor upon them by removing the harm that had befallen them, in place of gratitude to Him. This meaning has already appeared in al-An'am and Yunus, and will come in al-Isra'.

Al-Zajjaj said: this is specific to deception and disbelief, and he set the removal of harm against denial and disbelief. On this view, "min" in "minkum" is partitive (lil-tab'id), since the address is to people in general, and "the group" are the disbelievers. If the address is directed at the disbelievers, then "min" is explicative (lil-bayan).

The "lam" in ﴿that they may deny what We have given them﴾ is the lam of purpose (lam kay), that is: in order that they may deny what We have given them of the blessing of the removal of harm. So it is as though this denial on their part, which takes the place of the thanks that is obligatory upon them, is an aim and a goal among their aims. This is the extreme of obstinacy and stubbornness, beyond which there is nothing. It has been said that the lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), meaning that the outcome of those supplications was nothing but this disbelief.

Then He, glory be to Him, said, by way of threat and intimidation, shifting from the third person to the second person (iltifat): ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ So enjoy what you have of that. ﴿You will soon know﴾ the outcome of your affair, what will befall you in this world, and what you will come to in the Hereafter.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, related another type of their ugly deeds, saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share of what We have provided them.﴾ That is: this assigning occurs from them after they had cried out to Allah, glory be to Him, for the removal of harm from them, and after the disbelief and association with Him that follow the removal of harm. Yet despite this, they assign to what they do not know the reality of, namely inanimate objects and devils, a share of what We have provided them from their wealth, drawing near to them thereby.

It has also been said that the meaning is: they, that is the disbelievers, assign to the idols, while they know nothing because they are inanimate. On this view, the subject of "ya'lamun" (they know) is the idols, and they are treated as rational beings in their plural formation with the (masculine) plural suffix, in accordance with the disbelievers' belief concerning them.

The essential meaning is: these disbelievers assign to the idols, which do not understand anything, a share of their wealth which Allah has given them. ﴿By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.﴾ This is a return from the third person to the second person, and this questioning is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿About what you used to fabricate﴾ means what you invented of lies against Allah, glory be to Him, in this world.

﴿And they assign to Allah daughters.﴾ This is another kind of their scandals and ugly deeds. Khuza'ah and Kinanah used to say that the angels are the daughters of Allah, glory be to Him. He, glory be to Him, has exalted Himself above what these brutes attributed to Him, those who have no sound minds and no upright understanding: ﴿They are no more than cattle; rather, they are even more astray﴾ (al-Furqan 44). In this declaration of transcendence there is an expression of wonder at their condition. ﴿And for themselves is what they desire.﴾ That is: they assign to themselves what they desire of sons. The word "ma" is in the accusative position, governed by an implied verb, and it may also be in the nominative position as a subject (mubtada').

Al-Zajjaj rejected the accusative reading, saying: the Arabs do not say "ja'ala lahu kadha" (he made for him such-and-such) while meaning himself; rather they say "ja'ala li-nafsihi kadha" (he made for himself such-and-such). So if it were accusative, it would say "wa li-anfusihim ma yashtahun" (and for themselves what they desire).

But al-Farra' permitted the accusative reading.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned their aversion to the females whom they had assigned to Allah, saying: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female,﴾ that is, when one of them is informed of the birth of a daughter to him, ﴿his face becomes darkened,﴾ that is, changed. The intended meaning is not the blackness which is the opposite of whiteness, but rather a figurative use (kinayah) of blackness for dejection and change caused by the grief that results. The Arabs say of everyone who meets with something disagreeable: "his face has turned black with grief and sorrow." So said al-Zajjaj.

But al-Mawardi said: rather, the intended meaning is blackness of color in reality. He said: this is the view of the majority. The first view is more preferable, for it is known by experience that whoever becomes angry, grieved, or distressed does not have in his color anything but mere change and the appearance of gloominess and dejection, not real blackness. And the clause ﴿while he is suppressing [his rage].﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) (p-787), that is: full of grief, with suppressed anger and fury.

Al-Akhfash said: he is the one who suppresses his anger and does not show it. It has also been said that he is the one overcome with grief, whose mouth is closed from sorrow, derived from "al-kizamah," which is the sealing of the mouth of a well. This was said by Ali ibn Isa, and it has already been mentioned in Surah Yusuf.

﴿He hides himself from the people﴾ that is, he absconds and conceals himself, ﴿because of the ill of what he has been informed of.﴾ That is: because of the ill of grief, shame, and disgrace that befalls him by reason of the birth of a girl to him. ﴿Shall he keep it despite humiliation?﴾ That is: he remains continually wavering between two matters: either keeping the daughter he was informed of, or burying her in the dust, ﴿despite humiliation,﴾ that is, disgrace. So also did Isa al-Thaqafi read.

Al-Yazidi said: "al-hun" means humiliation in the dialect of Quraysh. So also did Abu Ubayd relate it from al-Kisa'i. And it is related from al-Kisa'i that it means affliction and hardship. Al-Khansa' said:

We humble souls, and the humbling of souls on the day of the terrible battle keeps them preserved.

Al-Farra' said: "al-hun" means "little" in the dialect of Tamim.

Al-Nahhas related from al-A'mash that he read: "Shall he keep it in disgrace, or bury it in the dust?" That is, hide it in the dust by burying it alive, as the Arabs used to do. So the one who has been informed of the birth of a female remains wavering between these two matters. The masculine pronoun in "yumsikuhu" and "yadussuhu" is used, despite its referring to the female, in observance of the wording.

Al-Jahdari read: "Or bury her in the dust." It would necessarily follow that he reads "Shall he keep her" (yumsikuha). It has also been said that "dass" (burying) means concealing her from people, so that she is not recognized, like something hidden because it is concealed from sight.

﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge.﴾ For they attributed the daughters, whom they dislike, to Allah, glory be to Him, and they attributed the sons, whom they love, to themselves. A similar statement is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That would be an unjust division﴾ (al-Najm 21–22).

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the attribute of evil.﴾ That is: for those whom Allah, glory be to Him, has described with these monstrous ugly qualities, is the attribute of evil, that is, the quality of evil, consisting of ignorance and disbelief in Allah. It has also been said that it is their description of Allah, glory be to Him, with a consort and a child. It has also been said that it is their need for a son to take their place, and the burying of daughters to avert shame and fear of poverty. It has also been said that it is punishment and the Fire. ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest attribute.﴾ That is the opposite of the attributes of created beings: complete wealth, all-encompassing generosity, and vast knowledge. Or it is oneness and sincerity in worship. Or it is that He is the Creator, the Provider, the Powerful, the Requiter. It has also been said that it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. And it has been said: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the parable of His light﴾ (al-Nur 35). ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, whom none can overpower, so their attributing to Him what is not befitting Him does Him no harm. ﴿The Wise﴾ in His acts and His sayings.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on surah 16, verses 51–68 (part 2 of 2):

Then, after Allah, glorified is He, related the great extent of the people's disbelief, He explained the breadth of His generosity and forbearance, in that He did not hasten to punish them and did not seize them for their wrongdoing. So He said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing﴾. By "the people" here is meant the disbelievers, or all the sinners. ﴿He would not leave upon it﴾, meaning upon the earth, even though it is not mentioned, for it is indicated by the mention of "the people" and the mention of "the creature" (*dābbah*). All of them are settled upon the earth. By "the creature" is meant the disbeliever, and it was said that it means everything that crawls. It has been asked, on this view: how can destruction encompass all of them when some of them have no sin? It is answered: the wrongdoer is destroyed as retribution against him, and the destruction of others, if they are among those who bear obligation, is for the sake of increasing their reward; and if they are from among others, then it is due to the evil consequence of the wrongdoing of the wrongdoers. And to Allah belongs the perfect wisdom. ﴿He is not asked about what He does, but they will be asked﴾ [al-Anbiya': 23]. A similar statement is His saying: ﴿And fear a trial which will not strike exclusively those of you who have done wrong﴾ [al-Anfal: 25].

Among the ḥadīths with this meaning is what is in Muslim and others, from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah intends a punishment for a people, the punishment strikes whoever is among them; then they will be raised according to their intentions." Likewise is the ḥadīth of the army that will be swallowed up in the desert, and at its end: that they will be raised according to their intentions. We have already presented, in the commentary on His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And fear a trial﴾ [al-Anfal: 25], and the verse, a genuine verification deserving of reference to it.

﴿But He delays them until a specified term﴾, known to Him, which is the end of their lives and the expiry of their lifespans, or the term of their punishment. In this delay there is profound wisdom, among which is establishing the proof against them (*al-iʿdhār*) and giving them latitude (*irkhāʾ al-ʿinān maʿahum*), and among which is the coming into being of those whom He foreknew from their offspring. ﴿So when their term comes﴾, which He has appointed for them, the word of Allah, glorified is He, will be fulfilled against them at that time, without advancing beyond it or delaying from it. The *sāʿah* is a short period of time, and its explanation and verification have already been presented.

Then He mentioned another type of their ignorance and foolishness, so He said: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾, meaning they ascribe to Him, glorified is He, what they dislike to be ascribed to themselves, namely daughters. This is a repetition of what has already been mentioned, for the purpose of emphasis and confirmation, and to increase the rebuke and reproach. ﴿And their tongues describe the lie﴾. This is from the other type which He, glorified is He, mentioned of their ugly deeds, and it is: that is, what their tongues describe of falsehood is their saying: ﴿that for them is the best﴾, i.e., the best attribute or the best outcome.

Al-Zajjaj said: they claim that they have, along with the ugliness of their statement, the good reward from Allah.

Al-Zajjaj also said, and al-Farrāʾ: ﴿that for them is the best﴾ is in apposition to ﴿their tongues describe the lie﴾, and *al-kadhib* (the lie) is in the accusative as the object of *taṣif* (describe).

Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, Mujāhid, and Ibn Muḥaysin read *al-kudhub* (with the *kāf*, *dhāl*, and *bāʾ* all vowelled with *ḍamma*), as an adjective to *al-alsun* (the tongues), and it is the plural of *kadhib*. In that case, the object according to this reading is ﴿that for them is the best﴾.

Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted them with His saying: ﴿Without doubt, for them is the Fire﴾, i.e., truly, for them, in place of what they assigned to themselves of the best, is the Fire. The verification of this has already been presented. ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾. Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Abū ʿUbaydah said: meaning, left behind and forgotten in the Fire. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ also said this, and so it is derived from "I *afraṭtu* so-and-so behind me," when I left him behind and forgot him.

Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: hastened toward it, sent forward into entering it, from "I *afraṭtuhu*," meaning I sent him ahead in seeking water. The *fāriṭ* is the one who goes ahead to the water, and the *furrāṭ* are those who go ahead in seeking water, and the *wurrād* are those who come later. From this is His saying (ﷺ): "I am your *faraṭ* at the Pool," meaning your one who goes ahead.

Al-Quṭāmī said:
*fa-staʿjalūnā wa-kānū min ṣaḥābatinā*
*kamā taʿajjala furrāṭun li-wurrādi*

Nāfiʿ, in the narration of Warsh, read *mufriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling (*wa-takhfīfihā*). This is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, and its meaning is: those who are extravagant in sins and disobediences. It is said: "So-and-so *afraṭa* over so-and-so" when he exceeded him and said to him more of the evil than he had said.

Abū Jaʿfar al-Qārī read *mufarriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and doubling it, meaning: those who neglect the command of Allah, so it is from *tafrīṭ* (neglect) regarding what is obligatory.

The rest read *mufraṭūn* with a *fatḥa* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling, and its meaning is: those sent ahead to the Fire.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid, regarding His saying: ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "The religion" is sincerity (*al-ikhlāṣ*), and *wāṣiban* means perpetual.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Abū Ṣāliḥ, regarding ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "There is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding *wāṣiban*: "perpetual."

Al-Firyābī and Ibn Jarīr transmitted from him: "obligatory."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿you cry out﴾: "you humbly supplicate with supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī: "you cry out in supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan regarding His saying: ﴿So enjoy, for you will soon know﴾: "It is a threat."

Ibn Jarīr transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know﴾, the verse: "They know that Allah created them, harms them and benefits them, and then they assign to what they do not know that it harms them and does not benefit them" ﴿a portion of what We have provided for them﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse: "They are the polytheists of the Arabs, who assigned to their idols and their devils a portion of what Allah had provided them, and set aside a part of their wealth, making it for their idols and their devils."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding the verse: "It is their saying: 'This is for Allah, according to their claim, and this is for our partners.'"

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to Allah daughters﴾, the verse: He says: "They assign to Me daughters, which they approve for Me but do not approve for themselves. That is because in the Jāhiliyyah, when a daughter was born to one of them, he kept her in humiliation, or buried her alive in the dust."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿And for them is what they desire﴾, he said: "It refers to sons."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Or does he bury it in the dust﴾, he said: "He buries his daughter alive."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge﴾, he said: "Evil is what they judged. He says: a thing they do not approve for themselves, so how would they approve it for Me?"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "It is the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "He says: there is nothing like Him."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿He has not left upon it any creature﴾, he said: "(i.e., He did not) give them rain."

He also transmitted from al-Suddī something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse, he said: "This was done in the time of Noah. Allah destroyed everything upon the surface of the earth of creatures, except what was carried in His ark."

Aḥmad in *al-Zuhd* transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "The sins of the son of Adam killed the dung beetle in its hole." Then he said: "By Allah, (this was) at the time of the drowning of the people of Noah."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from him: "The dung beetle was almost punished in its hole for the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted something similar from Anas.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, Ibn Jarīr, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from Abū Hurayrah that he heard a man say: "Indeed, the wrongdoer harms only himself." Abū Hurayrah said: "Yes, by Allah, indeed the bustard dies of emaciation in its nest because of the oppression of the oppressor."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk regarding ﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike﴾, he said: "They assign to Me daughters, and they dislike that for themselves."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best﴾, he said: "The statement of the disbelievers of Quraysh to us: 'For us are the sons, and for Him are the daughters.'"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah something similar.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾, he said: "Forgotten."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah, who said: "Hastened."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 16, verses 51–68 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glory be to Him, made clear that His created beings, both celestial and terrestrial, are subject to Him and humbled before His majesty, He followed this with a prohibition of association (shirk) in His words: ﴿And Allah said, "Do not take two gods. He is but one God."﴾ So He forbade taking two gods, then affirmed that divinity (al-ilahiyyah) is confined to one God, who is Allah, glory be to Him. It has been said that the dual form in "two gods" (ilahayn) indicates duality, and the singular in "God" (ilah) indicates unity. So what is the reason for describing "two gods" with "two" (ithnayn), and describing "God" with "one" (wahid)? The answer given is that there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir, rearrangement of words) in the speech, and the sense is: "Do not take two gods; He is only one God." It has also been said that the repetition is for the sake of emphasis in warning against taking a partner. It has also been said that the benefit of adding "two" is to make known that the prohibition concerns plurality and not the kind, and the benefit of adding "one" is to repel the supposition that the intent is only to affirm divinity without oneness, even though divinity itself is conceded to Him, glory be to Him, and the disagreement of the polytheists concerns only His oneness.

Then, by way of iltifat (shift from third person to first person), He, glory be to Him, moved the speech from the third person to the first person in order to increase the intimidation, saying: ﴿So it is Me that you should fear.﴾ That is: if you fear anything, then fear Me alone, not anyone else. The like of this has already passed at the beginning of al-Baqarah.

Then, when He had established His oneness, and that He is the One who must be singled out with fear and with hope directed to Him, He mentioned that all things are in His possession and under His disposal, saying: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This sentence confirms what came earlier in His words: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ (al-Nahl 49), to its end. The placing of the predicate first (taqdim al-khabar) serves to indicate exclusivity. ﴿And for Him is religion, constant.﴾ That is: established, obligatory, perpetual, not ceasing. Religion here means obedience and sincerity. Al-Farra' said: "wasiban" means "perpetual." From this is the verse of Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali:

I do not seek praise whose endurance is brief,
at the price of blame that lasts the whole age, perpetual.

That is: perpetual.

It is also narrated from al-Farra' that he said: "al-wasib" means "the sincere." But the first (meaning) is preferable. From this is His statement: ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾ (al-Saffat 9), that is, lasting.

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, obedience to Him is obligatory forever. Thus he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the obligatory."

Ibn Qutaybah said, in interpreting "al-wasib": no one is obeyed except that this (obedience) ceases through departure or destruction, except Allah, the Exalted, for obedience to Him endures. So he interpreted "al-wasib" as "the enduring." When a thing endures without ceasing, it becomes binding and established. It is said: "wasaba al-shay'u yasibu wusuban, fahuwa wasib," meaning it lasted; and "wasaba al-rajulu 'ala al-amr," meaning he persisted in it. It has also been said that "al-wasab" is fatigue and weariness, meaning that obedience to Allah, glory be to Him, is obligatory even if the servant becomes weary in it. But this does not suit what is in the verse.

The interrogative in His words: ﴿Then is it other than Allah you fear?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach, and it is coordinated with an implied element, as in its counterparts. The meaning is: since religion, that is obedience, is obligatory for Him permanently without ceasing, it is fitting to restrict piety (taqwa) to Him and not to direct it to anyone else.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, bestowed favor upon them by stating that all the blessings in which they live come from Him and not from anyone else. He said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah.﴾ That is: whatever blessings come upon you, of their various kinds, are from Allah, that is, they are from Him. Thus "ma" may be conditional (shartiyyah), and it may also be relative (mawsulah) with the sense of a condition, with "bikum" as its complement. "Min ni'mah" is either a circumstantial element (hal) from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase, or an explanation (bayan) of "ma." His words ﴿then from Allah﴾ are the predicate. If "ma" is conditional, the verb of the condition is elided, that is, "ma yakun" (whatever may be). Blessing is either religious, which is knowledge of the truth for its own sake and knowledge of the good for the sake of acting upon it; or worldly, which is either psychological, physical or external, such as material prosperity and other things. Each of these is a genus under which there are countless kinds, and all of them are from Allah, glory be to Him. So the intelligent person should give thanks to none but Him.

Then He explained the fickleness of the human being after he is immersed in the sea of blessings, saying: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help.﴾ That is: when harm touches you, of any kind, you turn to Allah, glory be to Him, and not to anyone else, humbly seeking its removal, for there is no remover of it but Him. It is said: "ja'ara yaj'aru" in the language of the Arabs, "ju'aran," meaning he raised his voice in humble supplication.

Al-A'sha said, describing a cow:

She circled three times between day and night,
and the reproach was that she should circle and cry out.

Harm (al-durr) means illness, affliction, need, drought, and everything by which a person is harmed.

﴿Then when He removes the harm from you, behold, a group of you associate others with their Lord.﴾ That is: when He removes from you the harm that had befallen you, behold, a group among you, those whose harm has been removed, associate others with their Lord, placing with Him another god, such as an idol or the like. The verse is brought to express wonder at the conduct of these people, who place partnership with Allah, who bestowed favor upon them by removing the harm that had befallen them, in place of gratitude to Him. This meaning has already appeared in al-An'am and Yunus, and will come in al-Isra'.

Al-Zajjaj said: this is specific to deception and disbelief, and he set the removal of harm against denial and disbelief. On this view, "min" in "minkum" is partitive (lil-tab'id), since the address is to people in general, and "the group" are the disbelievers. If the address is directed at the disbelievers, then "min" is explicative (lil-bayan).

The "lam" in ﴿that they may deny what We have given them﴾ is the lam of purpose (lam kay), that is: in order that they may deny what We have given them of the blessing of the removal of harm. So it is as though this denial on their part, which takes the place of the thanks that is obligatory upon them, is an aim and a goal among their aims. This is the extreme of obstinacy and stubbornness, beyond which there is nothing. It has been said that the lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), meaning that the outcome of those supplications was nothing but this disbelief.

Then He, glory be to Him, said, by way of threat and intimidation, shifting from the third person to the second person (iltifat): ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ So enjoy what you have of that. ﴿You will soon know﴾ the outcome of your affair, what will befall you in this world, and what you will come to in the Hereafter.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, related another type of their ugly deeds, saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share of what We have provided them.﴾ That is: this assigning occurs from them after they had cried out to Allah, glory be to Him, for the removal of harm from them, and after the disbelief and association with Him that follow the removal of harm. Yet despite this, they assign to what they do not know the reality of, namely inanimate objects and devils, a share of what We have provided them from their wealth, drawing near to them thereby.

It has also been said that the meaning is: they, that is the disbelievers, assign to the idols, while they know nothing because they are inanimate. On this view, the subject of "ya'lamun" (they know) is the idols, and they are treated as rational beings in their plural formation with the (masculine) plural suffix, in accordance with the disbelievers' belief concerning them.

The essential meaning is: these disbelievers assign to the idols, which do not understand anything, a share of their wealth which Allah has given them. ﴿By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.﴾ This is a return from the third person to the second person, and this questioning is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿About what you used to fabricate﴾ means what you invented of lies against Allah, glory be to Him, in this world.

﴿And they assign to Allah daughters.﴾ This is another kind of their scandals and ugly deeds. Khuza'ah and Kinanah used to say that the angels are the daughters of Allah, glory be to Him. He, glory be to Him, has exalted Himself above what these brutes attributed to Him, those who have no sound minds and no upright understanding: ﴿They are no more than cattle; rather, they are even more astray﴾ (al-Furqan 44). In this declaration of transcendence there is an expression of wonder at their condition. ﴿And for themselves is what they desire.﴾ That is: they assign to themselves what they desire of sons. The word "ma" is in the accusative position, governed by an implied verb, and it may also be in the nominative position as a subject (mubtada').

Al-Zajjaj rejected the accusative reading, saying: the Arabs do not say "ja'ala lahu kadha" (he made for him such-and-such) while meaning himself; rather they say "ja'ala li-nafsihi kadha" (he made for himself such-and-such). So if it were accusative, it would say "wa li-anfusihim ma yashtahun" (and for themselves what they desire).

But al-Farra' permitted the accusative reading.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned their aversion to the females whom they had assigned to Allah, saying: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female,﴾ that is, when one of them is informed of the birth of a daughter to him, ﴿his face becomes darkened,﴾ that is, changed. The intended meaning is not the blackness which is the opposite of whiteness, but rather a figurative use (kinayah) of blackness for dejection and change caused by the grief that results. The Arabs say of everyone who meets with something disagreeable: "his face has turned black with grief and sorrow." So said al-Zajjaj.

But al-Mawardi said: rather, the intended meaning is blackness of color in reality. He said: this is the view of the majority. The first view is more preferable, for it is known by experience that whoever becomes angry, grieved, or distressed does not have in his color anything but mere change and the appearance of gloominess and dejection, not real blackness. And the clause ﴿while he is suppressing [his rage].﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) (p-787), that is: full of grief, with suppressed anger and fury.

Al-Akhfash said: he is the one who suppresses his anger and does not show it. It has also been said that he is the one overcome with grief, whose mouth is closed from sorrow, derived from "al-kizamah," which is the sealing of the mouth of a well. This was said by Ali ibn Isa, and it has already been mentioned in Surah Yusuf.

﴿He hides himself from the people﴾ that is, he absconds and conceals himself, ﴿because of the ill of what he has been informed of.﴾ That is: because of the ill of grief, shame, and disgrace that befalls him by reason of the birth of a girl to him. ﴿Shall he keep it despite humiliation?﴾ That is: he remains continually wavering between two matters: either keeping the daughter he was informed of, or burying her in the dust, ﴿despite humiliation,﴾ that is, disgrace. So also did Isa al-Thaqafi read.

Al-Yazidi said: "al-hun" means humiliation in the dialect of Quraysh. So also did Abu Ubayd relate it from al-Kisa'i. And it is related from al-Kisa'i that it means affliction and hardship. Al-Khansa' said:

We humble souls, and the humbling of souls on the day of the terrible battle keeps them preserved.

Al-Farra' said: "al-hun" means "little" in the dialect of Tamim.

Al-Nahhas related from al-A'mash that he read: "Shall he keep it in disgrace, or bury it in the dust?" That is, hide it in the dust by burying it alive, as the Arabs used to do. So the one who has been informed of the birth of a female remains wavering between these two matters. The masculine pronoun in "yumsikuhu" and "yadussuhu" is used, despite its referring to the female, in observance of the wording.

Al-Jahdari read: "Or bury her in the dust." It would necessarily follow that he reads "Shall he keep her" (yumsikuha). It has also been said that "dass" (burying) means concealing her from people, so that she is not recognized, like something hidden because it is concealed from sight.

﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge.﴾ For they attributed the daughters, whom they dislike, to Allah, glory be to Him, and they attributed the sons, whom they love, to themselves. A similar statement is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That would be an unjust division﴾ (al-Najm 21–22).

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the attribute of evil.﴾ That is: for those whom Allah, glory be to Him, has described with these monstrous ugly qualities, is the attribute of evil, that is, the quality of evil, consisting of ignorance and disbelief in Allah. It has also been said that it is their description of Allah, glory be to Him, with a consort and a child. It has also been said that it is their need for a son to take their place, and the burying of daughters to avert shame and fear of poverty. It has also been said that it is punishment and the Fire. ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest attribute.﴾ That is the opposite of the attributes of created beings: complete wealth, all-encompassing generosity, and vast knowledge. Or it is oneness and sincerity in worship. Or it is that He is the Creator, the Provider, the Powerful, the Requiter. It has also been said that it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. And it has been said: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the parable of His light﴾ (al-Nur 35). ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, whom none can overpower, so their attributing to Him what is not befitting Him does Him no harm. ﴿The Wise﴾ in His acts and His sayings.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on surah 16, verses 51–68 (part 2 of 2):

Then, after Allah, glorified is He, related the great extent of the people's disbelief, He explained the breadth of His generosity and forbearance, in that He did not hasten to punish them and did not seize them for their wrongdoing. So He said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing﴾. By "the people" here is meant the disbelievers, or all the sinners. ﴿He would not leave upon it﴾, meaning upon the earth, even though it is not mentioned, for it is indicated by the mention of "the people" and the mention of "the creature" (*dābbah*). All of them are settled upon the earth. By "the creature" is meant the disbeliever, and it was said that it means everything that crawls. It has been asked, on this view: how can destruction encompass all of them when some of them have no sin? It is answered: the wrongdoer is destroyed as retribution against him, and the destruction of others, if they are among those who bear obligation, is for the sake of increasing their reward; and if they are from among others, then it is due to the evil consequence of the wrongdoing of the wrongdoers. And to Allah belongs the perfect wisdom. ﴿He is not asked about what He does, but they will be asked﴾ [al-Anbiya': 23]. A similar statement is His saying: ﴿And fear a trial which will not strike exclusively those of you who have done wrong﴾ [al-Anfal: 25].

Among the ḥadīths with this meaning is what is in Muslim and others, from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah intends a punishment for a people, the punishment strikes whoever is among them; then they will be raised according to their intentions." Likewise is the ḥadīth of the army that will be swallowed up in the desert, and at its end: that they will be raised according to their intentions. We have already presented, in the commentary on His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And fear a trial﴾ [al-Anfal: 25], and the verse, a genuine verification deserving of reference to it.

﴿But He delays them until a specified term﴾, known to Him, which is the end of their lives and the expiry of their lifespans, or the term of their punishment. In this delay there is profound wisdom, among which is establishing the proof against them (*al-iʿdhār*) and giving them latitude (*irkhāʾ al-ʿinān maʿahum*), and among which is the coming into being of those whom He foreknew from their offspring. ﴿So when their term comes﴾, which He has appointed for them, the word of Allah, glorified is He, will be fulfilled against them at that time, without advancing beyond it or delaying from it. The *sāʿah* is a short period of time, and its explanation and verification have already been presented.

Then He mentioned another type of their ignorance and foolishness, so He said: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾, meaning they ascribe to Him, glorified is He, what they dislike to be ascribed to themselves, namely daughters. This is a repetition of what has already been mentioned, for the purpose of emphasis and confirmation, and to increase the rebuke and reproach. ﴿And their tongues describe the lie﴾. This is from the other type which He, glorified is He, mentioned of their ugly deeds, and it is: that is, what their tongues describe of falsehood is their saying: ﴿that for them is the best﴾, i.e., the best attribute or the best outcome.

Al-Zajjaj said: they claim that they have, along with the ugliness of their statement, the good reward from Allah.

Al-Zajjaj also said, and al-Farrāʾ: ﴿that for them is the best﴾ is in apposition to ﴿their tongues describe the lie﴾, and *al-kadhib* (the lie) is in the accusative as the object of *taṣif* (describe).

Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, Mujāhid, and Ibn Muḥaysin read *al-kudhub* (with the *kāf*, *dhāl*, and *bāʾ* all vowelled with *ḍamma*), as an adjective to *al-alsun* (the tongues), and it is the plural of *kadhib*. In that case, the object according to this reading is ﴿that for them is the best﴾.

Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted them with His saying: ﴿Without doubt, for them is the Fire﴾, i.e., truly, for them, in place of what they assigned to themselves of the best, is the Fire. The verification of this has already been presented. ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾. Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Abū ʿUbaydah said: meaning, left behind and forgotten in the Fire. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ also said this, and so it is derived from "I *afraṭtu* so-and-so behind me," when I left him behind and forgot him.

Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: hastened toward it, sent forward into entering it, from "I *afraṭtuhu*," meaning I sent him ahead in seeking water. The *fāriṭ* is the one who goes ahead to the water, and the *furrāṭ* are those who go ahead in seeking water, and the *wurrād* are those who come later. From this is His saying (ﷺ): "I am your *faraṭ* at the Pool," meaning your one who goes ahead.

Al-Quṭāmī said:
*fa-staʿjalūnā wa-kānū min ṣaḥābatinā*
*kamā taʿajjala furrāṭun li-wurrādi*

Nāfiʿ, in the narration of Warsh, read *mufriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling (*wa-takhfīfihā*). This is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, and its meaning is: those who are extravagant in sins and disobediences. It is said: "So-and-so *afraṭa* over so-and-so" when he exceeded him and said to him more of the evil than he had said.

Abū Jaʿfar al-Qārī read *mufarriṭūn* with a *kasra* on the *rāʾ* and doubling it, meaning: those who neglect the command of Allah, so it is from *tafrīṭ* (neglect) regarding what is obligatory.

The rest read *mufraṭūn* with a *fatḥa* on the *rāʾ* and without doubling, and its meaning is: those sent ahead to the Fire.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid, regarding His saying: ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "The religion" is sincerity (*al-ikhlāṣ*), and *wāṣiban* means perpetual.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Abū Ṣāliḥ, regarding ﴿And for Him is the religion, constantly﴾. He said: "There is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding *wāṣiban*: "perpetual."

Al-Firyābī and Ibn Jarīr transmitted from him: "obligatory."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿you cry out﴾: "you humbly supplicate with supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī: "you cry out in supplication."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan regarding His saying: ﴿So enjoy, for you will soon know﴾: "It is a threat."

Ibn Jarīr transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know﴾, the verse: "They know that Allah created them, harms them and benefits them, and then they assign to what they do not know that it harms them and does not benefit them" ﴿a portion of what We have provided for them﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse: "They are the polytheists of the Arabs, who assigned to their idols and their devils a portion of what Allah had provided them, and set aside a part of their wealth, making it for their idols and their devils."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding the verse: "It is their saying: 'This is for Allah, according to their claim, and this is for our partners.'"

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿And they assign to Allah daughters﴾, the verse: He says: "They assign to Me daughters, which they approve for Me but do not approve for themselves. That is because in the Jāhiliyyah, when a daughter was born to one of them, he kept her in humiliation, or buried her alive in the dust."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿And for them is what they desire﴾, he said: "It refers to sons."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Or does he bury it in the dust﴾, he said: "He buries his daughter alive."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī regarding His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they judge﴾, he said: "Evil is what they judged. He says: a thing they do not approve for themselves, so how would they approve it for Me?"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "It is the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest example﴾, he said: "He says: there is nothing like Him."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿He has not left upon it any creature﴾, he said: "(i.e., He did not) give them rain."

He also transmitted from al-Suddī something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah regarding the verse, he said: "This was done in the time of Noah. Allah destroyed everything upon the surface of the earth of creatures, except what was carried in His ark."

Aḥmad in *al-Zuhd* transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "The sins of the son of Adam killed the dung beetle in its hole." Then he said: "By Allah, (this was) at the time of the drowning of the people of Noah."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from him: "The dung beetle was almost punished in its hole for the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature﴾.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā transmitted something similar from Anas.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, Ibn Jarīr, and al-Bayhaqī in *al-Shuʿab* transmitted from Abū Hurayrah that he heard a man say: "Indeed, the wrongdoer harms only himself." Abū Hurayrah said: "Yes, by Allah, indeed the bustard dies of emaciation in its nest because of the oppression of the oppressor."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk regarding ﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike﴾, he said: "They assign to Me daughters, and they dislike that for themselves."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid regarding His saying: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie, that for them is the best﴾, he said: "The statement of the disbelievers of Quraysh to us: 'For us are the sons, and for Him are the daughters.'"

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah something similar.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid regarding ﴿And that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾, he said: "Forgotten."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr something similar.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatādah, who said: "Hastened."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Ḥasan something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 16, verse 69 (part 1 of 2):

.
Allah, glorified is He, showed that the same conduct as that of Quraysh had occurred among all the other nations. He said, consoling His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿By Allah, We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you﴾, meaning messengers, ﴿but Satan made their deeds appear fair to them﴾, the evil deeds, ﴿so he is their guardian today﴾. It is possible that "today" refers to the time of this world, so the meaning is: he is their companion in this world. It is also possible that "today" refers to the Day of Resurrection and what follows it, so it refers to the coming state, and "guardian" (walī) means "helper." The intended meaning is the negation of any helper for them in the most emphatic way, because Satan cannot conceivably give them any help at all in the Hereafter. When the helper is restricted to him, it follows that there is no help from anyone else. It is also possible that "today" refers to some part of the time of this world, and this has two aspects. The first is that the intended part is the part that has passed, which is when Satan's adornment (of deeds) occurred for the earlier nations, so this is in the manner of narrating past states.
The second is that the intended part is the present part, which is the time of the revelation of this verse (p-٧٨٩).
The intended meaning is Satan's adornment (of deeds) for the disbelievers of Quraysh, so the pronoun in ﴿their guardian﴾ refers to the disbelievers of Quraysh, meaning: he is the guardian of these people today. Or it is by elision of a modifier, meaning: he is the guardian of the likes of those nations today. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾, meaning in the Hereafter, and it is the punishment of the Fire.
Then Allah, glorified is He, mentioned that whoever perished, perished only after the proof had been established against them and the excuse removed from them. He said: ﴿And We did not send down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾. This is an address to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and "the Book" is the Qur'an. The exception is an "istithna' mufarragh" (an exceptive construction lacking its object) from the most general of states, meaning: We did not send it down to you for any state nor for any cause except the cause of making it clear to them, that is, to the people, about what they differ over, from tawhid, the matters of resurrection, and all the legal rulings. The accusative of ﴿guidance and mercy﴾ is as two objects of purpose, coordinated with the position of "li-tubayyina" (in order that you may make clear). There is no need for the lam, because they are two actions of the agent of the action that is being explained, unlike "making clear," which is the action of the addressee and not the action of the One who sent down. ﴿For a people who believe﴾ in Allah, glorified is He, and who affirm what the messengers brought and what the books revealed.
Then Allah, glorified is He, returned to establishing His existence and His uniqueness in divinity by mentioning His great signs. He said: ﴿And Allah sent down from the sky water﴾, meaning from the clouds, that is, from the direction of above, as has passed, meaning a kind of water, ﴿and by it He brought the earth to life after its death﴾, meaning He brought it to life with vegetation after it had been dry with no life in it. ﴿Indeed in that﴾, the sending down and the giving of life, ﴿is a sign﴾, meaning an indication proving His oneness and His resurrection of creation and their recompense, ﴿for a people who listen﴾ to the speech of Allah and understand what it contains of lessons, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth.
﴿And indeed for you in the livestock is a lesson﴾. "Al-an'am" (livestock) are camels, cattle, and sheep, and goats are included among the sheep. "Ibrah" (lesson) originally means likening one thing to another so that its reality may be known by way of similarity, and from it comes ﴿so take warning, O people of insight﴾ [al-Hashr: 2]. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: the lesson in the livestock is their subjection to their owners and their obedience to them. The apparent meaning is that the lesson is His saying: ﴿We give you drink from what is in their bellies﴾, so the sentence is a new sentence explaining the lesson.
The people of Madina, Ibn 'Amir, and 'Asim in the transmission of Abu Bakr read "nusqikum" (We give you drink) with a fatha on the nun, from saqa yasqi.
The rest of the readers, and Hafs from 'Asim, read it with a damma on the nun, from asqa yasqi. It was said that they are two dialects.
Labid said:
"Saqa qawmi Bani Majdin wa-asqa Numayran wal-qaba'ila min Hilal"
[He gave drink to my people, the Banu Majd, and gave drink to Numayr and the tribes of Hilal.]
It was also read with a feminine (taa') prefix, on the basis that the pronoun refers back to the livestock, and it was read with a masculine (yaa') prefix, on the basis of returning the pronoun to Allah, glorified is He. Both are weak. All the readers in the first two readings agree. The fatha is the dialect of Quraysh and the damma is the dialect of Himyar. It was said that there is a difference between "saqa" and "asqa." When the drink passes from the hand of the one giving drink to the mouth of the one given drink, one says "saqaytuhu." If it is by merely presenting it to him and preparing it for him, one says "asqahu."
The pronoun in His saying ﴿from what is in their bellies﴾ refers back to the livestock.
Sibawayh said: the Arabs speak about the livestock using the predicate of the singular.
Al-Zajjaj said: since the word for the collective may be masculine or feminine, one says "huwa al-an'am" (it, the livestock, masculine) and "hiya al-an'am" (she, the livestock, feminine), so it is permissible for the pronoun to return in the masculine.
Al-Kisa'i said its meaning is: from what is in the bellies of what we have mentioned. So on this view it refers back to what was mentioned.
Al-Farra' said: "and that is correct."
Al-Mubarrad said: this is common and frequent in the Qur'an, like His saying about the sun: ﴿This is my Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 78], meaning this rising thing, and likewise ﴿And I am sending them a gift﴾ [al-Naml: 35], then He said: ﴿So when [the messenger] came to Sulayman﴾ [al-Naml: 36], and He did not say "came" (feminine), because the meaning is "the thing we mentioned came." End of quote. And from this is His saying: ﴿No! Indeed it is a reminder, so whoever wills may remember it﴾ [Abasa: 11, 12]. And similar to it is the saying of the poet:
"Mithl al-firakh nifat hawasiluhu"
[Like the chicks whose crops are full]
He did not say "hawasiluha" (their crops, feminine). And the saying of another:
"Wa-tab ilqah al-lubani wa-barad"
[And the milk of the she-camels became good and cooled]
He did not say "wa-baridat" (feminine).
It is related from al-Kisa'i that the meaning is: from what is in the bellies of some of them, which are the females, because the males have no milk. Abu 'Ubayda also said this. It is related from al-Farra' that he said: "al-na'am" and "al-an'am" are one thing, which is masculine and feminine, and for this reason the Arabs say: "hadhihi na'amun warid" (this is a herd of camels, coming to water). So the pronoun returned to the word "na'am," which has the meaning of "al-an'am," and this is like the saying of al-Zajjaj. Ibn al-'Arabi preferred this and said: the masculine refers to the meaning of the collective, and the feminine refers to the meaning of the group. So He used the masculine here with regard to the word for the collective, and He used the feminine in Surat al-Mu'minun with regard to the word for the group. ﴿From between digestive contents and blood﴾. "Al-farth" is the dung that descends into the stomach, and when it leaves it is no longer called "farth." One says: "afratha al-karish" when the paunch has expelled what is in it.
The meaning is that the thing you eat becomes from it what is in the paunch, which is the farth, and from it becomes the blood, so its lowest part is farth, its upper part is blood, and its middle part is milk. The blood flows in the veins and the milk in the udders, and the farth remains as it is.
﴿Pure﴾, meaning free of the redness of the blood and the filth of the farth, after the two have been gathered in one container. ﴿Palatable to the drinkers﴾, meaning delicious and wholesome, not choking the one who drinks it. One says: "sa'a al-sharab yasu'u sawgan," meaning it was easy for it to enter the throat.
﴿And from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapes﴾. Ibn Jarir said: the estimate is "and from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapes [is that] which you take," so "ma" was elided, and His saying "from it" indicates its elision. It was also said that it is coordinated with the livestock, and the estimate is: "and indeed for you from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapes is a lesson." It is also permissible that it is coordinated with "mimma fi butunihi" (from what is in their bellies), meaning: We give you drink from what is in their bellies and from the fruits of the palm trees. It is also permissible that it is connected to an elided verb indicated by what precedes it, its estimate being: "and We give you drink from the fruits of the palm trees." On this view, ﴿you take from it an intoxicant﴾ is an explanation of the giving of drink and a disclosure of its reality. It is also permissible that it is connected to "tattakhidhuna" (you take), its estimate being "and from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapes is a fruit from which you take an intoxicant," and the repetition of the adverbial phrase, which is His saying "from it," is for emphasis, like your saying "Zayd is in the house, in it." The pronoun in "minhu" is mentioned because it refers back to what was mentioned, or to the elided modified noun, which is the juice, as if it were said: "and from the juice of the fruits of the palm trees and the grapes you take an intoxicant." "Sakar" is what intoxicates from wine, and "rizq hasan" (good provision) is everything that is eaten from these two trees, such as dates, date syrup, raisins, and vinegar. The revelation of this verse was before the prohibition of wine. It was also said that "sakar" is vinegar in the language of Abyssinia, and "rizq hasan" (p-٧٩٠) is the food from the two trees. It was also said: "sakar" is the sweet, lawful juice, and it was called "sakar" because it may become intoxicating if it remains, so when it reaches intoxication it becomes forbidden.
The first view is preferable and is the view of the majority, and the lexicographers have stated explicitly that "sakar" is a name for wine. Only Abu 'Ubayda disagreed on this, for he said: "sakar" is food.
Among what supports the view of the majority of the lexicographers is the saying of the poet:
"Bi'sa al-sihab wa-bi'sa al-shurb shurbuhum * idha jara fihimu al-hadhyu wal-sakar"
[Evil are the companions, and evil is their drinking, when among them there runs the idle talk and the intoxicant.]
Among what supports the view of Abu 'Ubayda is what he recited:
"Ja'altu 'ayb al-akramina sakaran"
[I made the faults of the most noble into food]
That is, I made their blame food. Ibn Jarir preferred this and said: "sakar" is what is eaten of food, and what is lawful to drink from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapes, which is the good provision, so the wording differs and the meaning is one, like ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah﴾ [Yusuf: 86]. Al-Zajjaj said: this saying of Abu 'Ubayda is not known, and the people of tafsir are against it, and there is no proof in the verse he recited, because its meaning according to others is that it describes that they are covered with the faults of people. A group of the Hanafis interpreted "sakar" as what does not intoxicate from the nabidh (fermented drinks), and as what has lost two-thirds by boiling. They said: Allah only bestows favor on His servants by what He has made lawful for them, not by what He has forbidden them. This is rejected by the sound and mutawatir hadiths, on the assumption that it came after the verse of the prohibition of wine. End of quote.
﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason﴾, meaning a clear indication for whoever uses the intellect and acts by what it requires upon reflecting on the cosmic signs.
﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾. The discussion of revelation has already passed, and that it may mean inspiration, which is what He creates in the heart at the outset without an apparent cause. From it is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And [by] a soul and He who proportioned it and inspired it [with the knowledge of] its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ [al-Shams: 7, 8]. Among this is the inspiration of animals to do what benefits them and to avoid what harms them. Yahya ibn Wathhab read "ila al-nahal" with a fatha on the ha'.
Al-Zajjaj said: it was named "nahl" because Allah, glorified is He, gave it (nahalahu) the honey that comes out of it.
Al-Jawhari said: "al-nahl" and "al-nahla" are the bee, and it applies to the male and the female. ﴿That take for yourselves among the mountains houses﴾, meaning: that take, on the basis that "an" is the verbal "an" (that). It is also permissible that it be an explanatory "an," because in the revelation there is the meaning of saying. The pronoun in "ittakhidhi" (take, feminine) is feminine because it is one of the two permissible forms, as has passed, or for agreement with the meaning, or because "nahl" is a collective noun. The people of the Hijaz make "nahl" feminine. "Min" in ﴿among the mountains houses﴾ and likewise in ﴿among the trees﴾ and likewise in ﴿of what they erect﴾ is partitive, meaning dwellings suitable for it and fitting for it in the crevices of the mountains and the hollows of trees, and in the structures that the children of Adam erect from trellises, walls, and other things. "'Arsh" is used most often for what is made of wood. One says "'arrasha yu'arrishu" with kasra on the ra' or with damma.
The reading with damma is by Ibn 'Amir and Shu'ba.
The rest read with kasra.
It was also read "buyutan" with kasra on the ba' and with damma.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 16, verse 69 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Then eat of all the fruits﴾. Min (from) here is partitive (*li-l-tab'id*, indicating a part of the whole), because it eats the pollen of the trees. So when you eat, ﴿then follow the ways of your Lord﴾, meaning the paths that Allah has made you understand and taught you. He attributed them to the Lord because He is their Creator and the One who inspires the bee to follow them. The meaning is: enter the paths of your Lord to seek provision in the mountains and among the trees. Or it means: follow, in the ways of your Lord, what you have eaten, that is, in His courses in which, by His power, He turns the pollen into honey. Or, if you eat the fruits in distant places, then return to your hives ﴿following the ways of your Lord﴾ without going astray in them. The accusative *dhululan* (﻿ذُلُلًا, "submissively") is a circumstantial accusative (*hal*) relating to *al-subul* (the ways). It is the plural of *dhalul* (docile, made smooth), meaning made easy and not rugged. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Jarir chose this reading. It has also been said that it is a circumstantial accusative relating to the bees, meaning obedient to being subjected and to bringing forth honey from their bellies. Ibn Qutayba chose this reading. The clause ﴿there comes forth from their bellies﴾ is a new (resumed) sentence, shifted away from addressing the bees, in order to enumerate the blessings, to astonish every listener, to draw attention, and to guide to the great signs found in this creature, which resembles the fly. The "drink" in the verse is honey. The meaning of ﴿its colours vary﴾ is that some of it is white, some red, some blue and some yellow, according to the differences in the bees themselves, their colours and their foods.

Most of the exegetes hold that honey comes forth from the mouths of the bees. It has been said that it comes from their lower parts, and it has been said that it is not known from where in them it comes out. The pronoun in His words ﴿in it is healing for mankind﴾ refers to the drink that comes out of the bees' bellies, which is honey. This is the view of the majority.

Al-Farra', Ibn Kaysan and a group of the early scholars said that the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, and the sense would be: in what We have related to you of the signs and proofs there is healing for mankind. But there is no reason to depart from the apparent meaning, to oppose the clear referent and the manifest context.

The people of knowledge have differed as to whether this healing that Allah placed in honey is general for every disease or specific to some diseases. One group said it is general. Another group said it is specific to some diseases. The evidence for this is that *'asal* (honey) is an indefinite noun in an affirmative context, and so it is not general. Its indefiniteness, if it is intended to express magnitude, indicates only that there is great healing in it for a disease or diseases, not for every disease, since the indefiniteness of magnitude does not confer generality. What is apparent from experience and from the principles of the science of medicine is that when honey is used alone it is a remedy for specific diseases, and when it is mixed with other things, as in electuaries (*ma'ajin*) and the like, it becomes, together with what it is mixed with, a remedy for many diseases.

In sum, it is among the greatest of foods and the most beneficial of medicines, and these two qualities rarely come together in anything else. ﴿Indeed, in that﴾, the aforementioned matter of the bees, ﴿is a sign for a people who give thought﴾, that is, who employ their minds when considering the workmanship of Allah, glorified is He, and the wonders of His creatures. For the affair of the bees is among the most wondrous, strange, subtle and precise of these.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abu Dawud in his *Nasikh* (on abrogation, *naskh*), Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, al-Bayhaqi in his *Sunan*, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas that he was asked about His words ﴿You take from it intoxicant and good provision﴾, and he said: the intoxicant is what is forbidden from their fruits, and the good provision is what is lawful.

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him also, who said: the intoxicant is the forbidden thing, and the good provision is its raisins, its vinegar, its grapes and its benefits.

Abu Dawud in his *Nasikh* and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him, also, who said: the intoxicant is *nabidh* (date or raisin infusion), and the good provision is raisins, and this verse abrogated it: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90].

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi transmitted from him also, regarding the verse, that he said: Allah then forbade the intoxicant along with the forbidding of wine, because it is derived from it. Then He said ﴿and good provision﴾, and that is the lawful from vinegar, raisins, *nabidh* and the like. So Allah confirmed it and made it lawful for the Muslims.

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Umar that he was asked about the intoxicant, and he said: wine itself.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: the intoxicant is wine.

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee﴾, that he said: He inspired it.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿follow the ways of your Lord, made smooth﴾, that he said: paths upon which no place is rugged for the one who travels them.

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatadah regarding *dhululan* (﻿ذُلُلًا, "made smooth"), that he said: obedient.

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from al-Suddi, who said: docile.

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿There comes forth from their bellies a drink﴾, that he said: honey.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Mujahid regarding the verse, that he said: it is honey, in which there is healing, and in the Qur'an.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Honey is a healing from every disease, and the Qur'an is a healing for what is in the breasts."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Take upon yourselves the two cures: honey and the Qur'an."

Ibn Majah, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab*, Ibn al-Sunni, Abu Nu'aym and al-Khatib transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Take upon yourselves the two cures: honey and the Qur'an."

There are also traditions about honey being a healing. Among them is what al-Bukhari transmitted from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Healing is in three things: a cupping incision, a draught of honey, or a branding with fire; and I forbid my community from cauterization."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others transmitted from the hadith of Abu Sa'id that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my brother's bowels are loose." He said: "Give him honey to drink." So he gave him honey to drink, then came back and said: "I gave him honey and it only increased the looseness." He said: "Go and give him honey to drink." So he went and gave him to drink, then came back and said: "It only increased the looseness." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has spoken the truth and your brother's belly has lied. Go and give him honey to drink." So he went and gave him honey to drink, and he was cured.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 16, verses 70–74 (part 1 of 2):

.

When He, glorified is He, mentioned some conditions of animals and the wonders of marvelous craftsmanship within them, and the properties of overpowering power, He followed this with the wonders of the creation of man and the lessons within it, and so He said: ﴿And Allah created you﴾ when you were not anything, ﴿then He causes you to die﴾ at the completion of your terms, ﴿and among you is one who is returned to the most abject age﴾. It is said: radhala, yarduhu, radhalah, meaning he became base; al-ardhal (the most abject) and al-radhalah are the worst and lowliest of a thing.

Al-Naysaburi said: Know that the wise have fixed the stages of human life in four. The first is the age of growth (sin al-nushu').
The second is the age of standing firm, which is the age of youth (sin al-shabab).
The third is the age of slight decline, which is the age of middle age (sin al-kuhula).
The fourth is the age of manifest decline, which is the age of old age (sin al-shaykhukha).
It is said: the most abject age is when a person reaches senility (al-kharaf), which is that he becomes like the child who has no intellect. It is said it is seventy-five years, and it is said ninety years. A verse similar to this is His, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature; then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ [al-Tin: 4, 5]. Then, glorified is He, gave the reason for His returning whoever He returns to the most abject age with His saying: ﴿so that he will not know, after knowledge, anything﴾, meaning he had acquired some knowledge, neither much nor little, or some of the known things, if "knowledge" here means "the known." It is said the intended meaning of "knowledge" here is intellect. It is said the intended meaning is that he should not know anything in addition to the knowledge he had already acquired before that.

Then, when He, glorified is He, had explained the creation of man and his transformation through the stages of life, He mentioned a portion of his conditions, perhaps he would remember at that point, and so He said: ﴿And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision﴾, meaning He made you differ in it. So He widened provision for some of His servants until He gave him sustenance sufficient for thousands of the children of Adam gathered together, and He constricted it for some of His servants until he could find no food except by asking people and begging from them. This is for a profound wisdom whose depths the minds of servants fall short of grasping and of knowing the reality of its causes. And just as He made the difference among His servants in wealth, He made it among them in intellect, knowledge, understanding, bodily strength and weakness, beauty and ugliness, health and sickness, and other conditions.

It is said: the meaning of the verse is that Allah, glorified is He, gave the masters more than He gave their slaves, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿So those who were favoured would not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess, so that they would be equal therein﴾. That is, those whom Allah favoured with abundance of provision over others would not return their provision, which Allah gave them, to those slaves whom their right hands possess, such that they (the masters and the slaves) would be equal in it. Thus the particle "fa" (so) here indicates that equality is consequent upon returning, meaning: they do not return it to them in a manner that entails equality, but they return to them only a small portion of it. This is a parable Allah, glorified is He, struck for the worshippers of idols: that is, if your slaves are not equal with you and you are not pleased with that, then how do you make My slaves equal with Me, while your slaves are equal to you in humanness and createdness? Since you do not make your slaves partners with you in your wealth, how do you make some of the servants of Allah, glorified is He, partners with Him so that you worship them along with Him? Or how do you make some of His creatures, such as idols, partners with Him in worship? Ibn Jarir mentioned the meaning of this. [p. 792] A verse similar to this is His, glorified is He: ﴿He has set forth for you a parable from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you?﴾ [al-Rum: 28].

It is said that the "fa" in ﴿so they are equal therein﴾ means "until" (hatta): "Then is it the blessing of Allah that they deny?" In that you do what you do of associating partners. The blessing is His, glorified is He, making the owners superior to the owned. It has been read ﴿yajhadun﴾ with a yā' (third person) and with a tā' (second person).

Abu 'Ubayda and Abu Hatim said: The reading in the third person is preferable, because the one spoken of is near, and because if it were in the second person, its apparent address would be to the Muslims. The interrogation is for denunciation, and the "fa" is for coordination with an implied element, meaning: they associate partners with Him so they deny His blessing. The meaning according to the reading in the second person is that the owners are not those who return their provision to their slaves; rather, I am the One who provides for them and for them. So they should not think that they give them anything; it is only My provision that I cause to flow through their hands, and they are all equal in that, having no superiority over their slaves. Thus the implied element coordinated with would be a verb suited to this meaning, as if it were said: "They do not understand that, so they deny the blessing of Allah."

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the other state of man's conditions, and so He said: ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from among yourselves﴾. The exegetes said: meaning women, for He created Hawwa' from the rib of Adam. Or the meaning is: He created for you spouses from your own kind, so that you might find companionship in them, because a kind finds companionship with its own kind and is uneasy with other than its kind. Through this companionship occurs between men and women that which is the cause of offspring, which is the aim of marriage. For this reason He said: ﴿And He has made for you from your spouses sons and grandchildren (hafadah)﴾. Al-hafadah is the plural of hafid; it is said hafada yahfidu hafdan and hufudan: when he hastens. So everyone who hastens in service is a hafid. Abu 'Ubayd said: al-hafd is work and service.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: al-hafadah among the Arabs are servants, and from this is the verse of the poet, who is al-A'sha:
"You burdened our unknown with Yemeni she-camels, when the drivers on their backs hastened."
That is, the servants and helpers.

Al-Azhari said: It is said: the hafadah are the children of children. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas. It is said: the in-laws (al-akhtan), said by Ibn Mas'ud, 'Alqamah, Abu al-Duha, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. From this is the saying of the poet:
"Had my soul obeyed me, there would have become for her many a hafad among those counted."
"But it is a soul proud over me, averse to the in-laws of the base, abhorrent."
It is said: al-hafadah are the in-laws (al-aṣhār).

Al-Asma'i said: al-khatn is whoever is from the woman's side, like her son, her brother and the like, and al-aṣhār are from both of them together. It is said: so-and-so became in-laws (asharah) to the sons of so-and-so and intermarried (sahara). It is said: they are the children of a man's wife from another husband. It is said: they are the children who serve him. It is said: they are daughters serving their father.

Many scholars preferred that they are the children of children, because He, glorified is He, bestowed a favour upon His servants by making for them sons and grandchildren from their spouses. The grandchildren are apparently conjoined to the sons, though it is permissible that the meaning be: He made for you sons from your spouses and made for you grandchildren. But on this apparent meaning, it is not impossible that "sons" refers to those who do not serve, and "grandchildren" refers to those among them who serve the father; or "grandchildren" refers only to daughters. It indicates that they are the children of children only if the construction of the verse is: "And He made for you from your spouses sons, and from the sons grandchildren." ﴿And He has provided you from the good things﴾ which you find pleasant and enjoy.
