Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 16, verses 84–90 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glory be to Him, had explained the state of these people, that they recognised God's blessing and then denied it, and that most of them are disbelievers, He followed it with the various kinds of threat of the Day of Resurrection. He said: ﴿And [mention] the Day when We raise up from every nation a witness﴾. That is, mention the Day when We raise up, or [it means]: the Day when We raise up, they will fall into what they fell into. The witness of every nation is its prophet, who testifies for them to faith and affirmation, and against them to disbelief, denial and rejection. ﴿Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved﴾, that is, to make excuses, since they have no proof and no excuse, as in His statement, glory be to Him: ﴿Nor will they be permitted, so they could make excuse﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36]. Or [it means]: to speak at length. Or: to return to the worldly abode. The use of "then" (thumma) here indicates that their being afflicted with being prevented from making excuses, which indicates total despair, is more severe than their being afflicted with the testimony of the prophets. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾, because reproach (`itab) is only sought for the purpose of returning to good pleasure; so when there is a resolve of wrath, there is no benefit in reproach.

The meaning: they will not be asked to be pleased, that is, they will not be required to please their Lord, because the Hereafter is not an abode of obligation, and they will not be left to return to the world so that they might repent. The root of the word is from `atab, which means "to be aggrieved." It is said: `atiba `alayhi, ya`tibu, when he was aggrieved with him. When he pours upon him what he was aggrieved about, it is said `atabahu (he reproached him). When he returns to his gladness, it is said a`tabahu (he appeased him). The noun is al-`utba, which is the return of the one who was reproached to what pleases the reproacher. Al-Harawi said this, and from it is the saying of al-Nabigha:

"If I am wronged, [it is] a slave whom you have wronged; and if I have grievance, one like you appeases."

﴿And when those who wronged see the punishment﴾, that is, when those who associated partners [with God] see the punishment that they deserve for their polytheism, which is the punishment of Hell, that punishment will not be lightened for them ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾, that is, they will not be given respite to repent, since there is no repentance there.

﴿And when those who associated partners see their partners﴾, that is, their idols and images which they worshipped, because it has been established that they will be raised together with the polytheists, so that it will be said to them: "Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it," as established in the Sahih from the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿They will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You."﴾ That is, those whom we used to worship besides You.

Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: The intent of the polytheists in this statement is to shift the blame onto those idols, making excuses and seeking relief by it, while knowing that the punishment is inevitably befalling them; but the drowning person clutches at whatever his hand falls upon. ﴿Then they will throw to them the word﴾, that is, those idols, images, devils and the like will cast to the polytheists the word ﴿"Indeed, you are liars."﴾ That is, they will say to them: "Indeed you, O polytheists, are liars in what you claim of shifting the blame onto us, which is your intent in this statement."

If it is said: The polytheists pointed to the idols and the like, [saying] "These are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You," and they were truthful in that; so how did the idols and the like deny them? The answer: their meaning by saying "These are our partners" was: these are partners of God in being worshipped; so the idols denied them in claiming this partnership. The idols and images, although they cannot speak, God, glory be to Him, will make them speak in that state in order to shame and rebuke the polytheists. This is like what the angels said: ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾ [Saba': 41], meaning that the jinn were the ones who were pleased with their worship of them.

﴿And they will offer submission to God that Day﴾, that is, the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection will offer submission and compliance to His punishment and humility before His might. It was also said: the worshipper and the worshipped both submitted and complied with His judgment concerning them. ﴿And what they used to invent will be lost to them﴾, that is, what they used to fabricate, that God, glory be to Him, has partners, and what they used to claim of their intercession for them, and that their worship of them brings them nearer to God, glory be to Him, will perish and be void.

Those who disbelieved within themselves and barred others ﴿from the way of God﴾, that is, from the path of truth, which is the path of Islam and faith, by preventing them from following it and compelling them to disbelief. It was also said that what is meant by barring from the way of God is barring from the Sacred Mosque, but the more appropriate view is generality.

Then He informed about those who did this deed by His saying: ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾, that is, God will increase them in punishment for the sake of leading others astray, over and above the punishment they deserved for their own error. It was also said that the meaning is: We will increase the leaders in punishment over the punishment of their followers, that is, more severe than it. It was also said that this increase is their being brought out of the Fire to the zamharir (freezing cold). And other things have been said.

﴿And [mention] the Day when We raise up in every nation a witness against them﴾, that is, a prophet who testifies against them from among themselves, from their own kind, to complete the proof and cut off excuse. This is a repetition of what preceded, for the purpose of emphasis and warning. ﴿And We have brought you, O Muhammad, as a witness over these﴾, that is, you will bear witness over these nations and testify for them. It was also said: over your own nation. Something similar has already been mentioned in al-Baqarah and al-Nisa'. ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book﴾, that is, the Qur'an. The clause is either independent, or in the place of a circumstantial accusative with the implied qad. ﴿As an explanation of all things﴾, that is, a clarification of it. The ta' is for emphasis (intensive), and its parallel among verbal nouns is al-tilqa'; no other examples exist. A similar verse is His statement, glory be to Him: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾ [al-An`am: 38]. The meaning of it being an explanation of all things is that it contains clarification of many rulings, and for what remains of them it refers to the Sunnah; and He commanded them to follow His Messenger (ﷺ) in what he brings of rulings, and to obey him, as in the Qur'anic verses indicating this. It is authentically reported from him (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed I have been given the Qur'an and its like with it." And it is guidance and mercy for the servants (p-798) ﴿and good tidings for the Muslims﴾, specifically and to the exclusion of others; or the guidance, mercy and good tidings are specifically for them, since they are the ones who benefit from it.

Then, when He, glory be to Him, mentioned that in the Qur'an there is an explanation of all things, He followed it with a verse comprehensive of all the foundations of obligation, as confirmation of that, saying: ﴿Indeed, God commands justice and good conduct﴾.

The people of knowledge have differed in interpreting "justice" and "good conduct." It was said: justice is "there is no god but God," and good conduct is performing the obligations. It was said: justice is the obligatory, and good conduct is the supererogatory.

It was said: justice is the equality of the outward and the inward, and good conduct is that the inward be better than the outward.

It was said: justice is fairness, and good conduct is bestowing favour.

The more appropriate interpretation of justice is by its linguistic meaning, which is moderation between the two extremes of excess and deficiency. So the meaning of His command, glory be to Him, to justice is that His servants should be in a moderate state in religion, not inclining toward the side of excess, which is blameworthy extremism in religion, nor toward the side of deficiency, which is neglecting anything that is part of the religion. As for good conduct, its linguistic meaning indicates that it is bestowing favour with what is not obligatory, like voluntary charity; and among good conduct is doing what the servant is rewarded for, of what God has not made obligatory upon him, in acts of worship and other things. It is authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he explained good conduct as worshipping God as if you see Him. He said in the hadith of Ibn `Umar, which is established in the Two Sahihs: "Good conduct is that you worship God as if you see Him; and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you." This is the meaning of good conduct in the Shari`ah. ﴿And giving to close relatives﴾, that is, giving relatives what their need calls for. In the verse there is guidance to maintaining ties of kinship and encouragement to give charity to them. This is of the category of specific after general if giving to relatives has entered under justice and good conduct; and it was said it is of the category of mandub (recommended) being joined to wajib (obligatory). A similar verse is His statement: ﴿And give the close relative his right﴾. The reason He specified close relatives is that their right is more emphatic, for God has derived the name of the womb (rahim) from His own name, and made joining it part of His joining, and severing it part of His severing. ﴿And He forbids immorality﴾: it is the matter that increases in ugliness, in speech or deed. It was said it is fornication; it was said stinginess. And the munkar is what the Shari`ah has disapproved by prohibiting it, and it encompasses all sins across their varieties. It was also said it is polytheism. As for transgression (baghy), it was said to be arrogance, it was said wrongdoing, it was said malice, it was said aggression; its reality is exceeding the limit, so it includes those mentioned, and all its kinds fall under the munkar. It was singled out for mention out of concern for it, because of its severe harm and the evil of its consequence. It is among the sins that return upon their doer, as in His statement, glory be to Him: ﴿Your transgression is only against yourselves﴾ [Yunus: 23]. This verse is among the verses indicating the obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil. Then God, glory be to Him, concluded this verse with His statement: ﴿He admonishes you that you may be reminded﴾, that is, He admonishes you with what He has mentioned in this verse of what He has commanded you and forbidden you from, for it is sufficient in the matter of admonition and reminding. ("That you may be reminded") means: that you may remember what should be remembered, and so be admonished by what God has admonished you with.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatadah concerning His statement: ﴿And [mention] the Day when We raise up from every nation a witness﴾, he said: its witness is its prophet, that he conveyed the messages of his Lord. God said: ﴿And We have brought you as a witness over these﴾. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) when he recited this verse, his eyes would overflow.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj concerning ﴿And they will offer submission to God that Day﴾, he said: they submitted.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted similarly from Qatadah.

He said: ﴿And [mention] the Day when We raise up from every nation a witness﴾. The witness of every nation is its prophet, who testifies for them to faith and affirmation, and against them to disbelief, denial and rejection. ﴿Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved﴾, that is, to make excuses, since they have no proof and no excuse, as in His statement, glory be to Him: ﴿Nor will they be permitted, so they could make excuse﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36]. The root of the word is from `atab, which means "to be aggrieved." It is said: `atiba `alayhi, ya`tibu, when he was aggrieved with him. The noun is al-`utba, which is the return of the one who was reproached to what pleases the reproacher. Al-Harawi said this, and from it is the saying of al-Nabigha:

﴿And when those who wronged see the punishment﴾, that is, when those who associated partners [with God] see the punishment that they deserve for their polytheism, which is the punishment of Hell, that punishment will not be lightened for them ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾, that is, they will not be given respite to repent, since there is no repentance there.

﴿And when those who associated partners see their partners﴾, that is, their idols and images which they worshipped, because it has been established that they will be raised together with the polytheists, so that it will be said to them: "Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it," as established in the Sahih from the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ).

If it is said: The polytheists pointed to the idols and the like, [saying] "These are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You," and they were truthful in that; so how did the idols and the like deny them? The answer: their meaning by saying "These are our partners" was: these are partners of God in being worshipped; so the idols denied them in claiming this partnership. The idols and images, although they cannot speak, God, glory be to Him, will make them speak in that state in order to shame and rebuke the polytheists. This is like what the angels said: ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾ [Saba': 41], meaning that the jinn were the ones who were pleased with their worship of them.

﴿And they will offer submission to God that Day﴾, that is, the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection will offer submission and compliance to His punishment and humility before His might. It was also said: the worshipper and the worshipped both submitted and complied with His judgment concerning them. ﴿And what they used to invent will be lost to them﴾, that is, what they used to fabricate, that God, glory be to Him, has partners, and what they used to claim of their intercession for them, and that their worship of them brings them nearer to God, glory be to Him, will perish and be void.

Those who disbelieved within themselves and barred others ﴿from the way of God﴾, that is, from the path of truth, which is the path of Islam and faith, by preventing them from following it and compelling them to disbelief. It was also said that what is meant by barring from the way of God is barring from the Sacred Mosque, but the more appropriate view is generality.

Then He informed about those who did this deed by His saying: ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾, that is, God will increase them in punishment for the sake of leading others astray, over and above the punishment they deserved for their own error. It was also said that the meaning is: We will increase the leaders in punishment over the punishment of their followers, that is, more severe than it. It was also said that this increase is their being brought out of the Fire to the zamharir (freezing cold). And other things have been said.

﴿And [mention] the Day when We raise up in every nation a witness against them﴾, that is, a prophet who testifies against them from among themselves, from their own kind, to complete the proof and cut off excuse. This is a repetition of what preceded, for the purpose of emphasis and warning. ﴿And We have brought you, O Muhammad, as a witness over these﴾, that is, you will bear witness over these nations and testify for them. It was also said: over your own nation. Something similar has already been mentioned in al-Baqarah and al-Nisa'. ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book﴾, that is, the Qur'an. The clause is either independent, or in the place of a circumstantial accusative with the implied qad. ﴿As an explanation of all things﴾, that is, a clarification of it. The ta' is for emphasis (intensive), and its parallel among verbal nouns is al-tilqa'; no other examples exist. A similar verse is His statement, glory be to Him: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾ [al-An`am: 38]. The meaning of it being an explanation of all things is that it contains clarification of many rulings, and for what remains of them it refers to the Sunnah; and He commanded them to follow His Messenger (ﷺ) in what he brings of rulings, and to obey him, as in the Qur'anic verses indicating this. It is authentically reported from him (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed I have been given the Qur'an and its like with it." And it is guidance and mercy for the servants (p-798) ﴿and good tidings for the Muslims﴾, specifically and to the exclusion of others; or the guidance, mercy and good tidings are specifically for them, since they are the ones who benefit from it.

Then, when He, glory be to Him, mentioned that in the Qur'an there is an explanation of all things, He followed it with a verse comprehensive of all the foundations of obligation, as confirmation of that, saying: ﴿Indeed, God commands justice and good conduct﴾.

The people of knowledge have differed in interpreting "justice" and "good conduct." It was said: justice is "there is no god but God," and good conduct is performing the obligations. It was said: justice is the obligatory, and good conduct is the supererogatory.

It was said: justice is the equality of the outward and the inward, and good conduct is that the inward be better than the outward.

It was said: justice is fairness, and good conduct is bestowing favour.

The more appropriate interpretation of justice is by its linguistic meaning, which is moderation between the two extremes of excess and deficiency. So the meaning of His command, glory be to Him, to justice is that His servants should be in a moderate state in religion, not inclining toward the side of excess, which is blameworthy extremism in religion, nor toward the side of deficiency, which is neglecting anything that is part of the religion. As for good conduct, its linguistic meaning indicates that it is bestowing favour with what is not obligatory, like voluntary charity; and among good conduct is doing what the servant is rewarded for, of what God has not made obligatory upon him, in acts of worship and other things. It is authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he explained good conduct as worshipping God as if you see Him. He said in the hadith of Ibn `Umar, which is established in the Two Sahihs: "Good conduct is that you worship God as if you see Him; and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you." This is the meaning of good conduct in the Shari`ah. ﴿And giving to close relatives﴾, that is, giving relatives what their need calls for. In the verse there is guidance to maintaining ties of kinship and encouragement to give charity to them. This is of the category of specific after general if giving to relatives has entered under justice and good conduct; and it was said it is of the category of mandub (recommended) being joined to wajib (obligatory). A similar verse is His statement: ﴿And give the close relative his right﴾. The reason He specified close relatives is that their right is more emphatic, for God has derived the name of the womb (rahim) from His own name, and made joining it part of His joining, and severing it part of His severing. ﴿And He forbids immorality﴾: it is the matter that increases in ugliness, in speech or deed. It was said it is fornication; it was said stinginess. And the munkar is what the Shari`ah has disapproved by prohibiting it, and it encompasses all sins across their varieties. It was also said it is polytheism. As for transgression (baghy), it was said to be arrogance, it was said wrongdoing, it was said malice, it was said aggression; its reality is exceeding the limit, so it includes those mentioned, and all its kinds fall under the munkar. It was singled out for mention out of concern for it, because of its severe harm and the evil of its consequence. It is among the sins that return upon their doer, as in His statement, glory be to Him: ﴿Your transgression is only against yourselves﴾ [Yunus: 23]. This verse is among the verses indicating the obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil. Then God, glory be to Him, concluded this verse with His statement: ﴿He admonishes you that you may be reminded﴾, that is, He admonishes you with what He has mentioned in this verse of what He has commanded you and forbidden you from, for it is sufficient in the matter of admonition and reminding. ("That you may be reminded") means: that you may remember what should be remembered, and so be admonished by what God has admonished you with.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatadah concerning His statement: ﴿And [mention] the Day when We raise up from every nation a witness﴾, he said: its witness is its prophet, that he conveyed the messages of his Lord. God said: ﴿And We have brought you as a witness over these﴾. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) when he recited this verse, his eyes would overflow.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Mujahid concerning His statement: ﴿Then they will throw to them the word﴾, he said: they will speak to them.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Jurayj concerning ﴿And they will offer submission to God that Day﴾, he said: they submitted.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted similarly from Qatadah.

`Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad ibn al-Sarri, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim (who declared it sahih), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba`th wa'l-Nushur transmitted from Ibn Mas`ud concerning His statement: ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾, he said: they will be increased scorpions with fangs like tall palm trees.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib transmitted from al-Bara' that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the statement of God, exalted be He: ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾, so he said: "Scorpions like tall palm trees, which sting them in Hell."

Abu Ya`la, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn `Abbas concerning His statement: ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾, he said: five rivers of fire which God pours upon them, by which they are punished, some of them by night and some of them by day.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Jabir from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The increase is five rivers flowing from beneath the Throne upon the heads of the people of the Fire: three rivers according to the measure of the night, and two rivers according to the measure of the day; therefore this is His statement: ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Mas`ud that he said: Indeed God has sent down in this Book an explanation of all things, but our knowledge falls short of what has been made clear to us in the Qur'an. Then he recited: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾.

Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, `Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Zuhd, Ibn al-Duraysi in Fada'il al-Qur'an, Muhammad ibn Nasr in Kitab al-Salah, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab transmitted from Ibn Mas`ud that he said: Whoever desires knowledge, let him probe the Qur'an deeply, for in it is the knowledge of the first and the last.

Ahmad transmitted from `Uthman ibn Abi al-`As, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when his gaze became fixed, and he said: "Gabriel came to me and commanded me to place this verse in this position of the surah": ﴿Indeed, God commands justice and good conduct﴾ to the end of the verse.

In its chain is Shahr ibn Hawshab.

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir: its chain is not objectionable.

Ahmad, al-Bukhari in al-Adab, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it at greater length from the hadith of Ibn `Abbas, and Ibn Kathir rated its chain as hasan.

Al-Bawardi, Ibn al-Sakan, Ibn Mandah, and Abu Nu'aym in *Ma'rifat al-Sahabah* narrated from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr that when this verse reached Aktham ibn Sayfi, the sage of the Arabs, he said: "I see that it commands noble character and forbids what is contrary to it." Then he said to his people: "Be leaders in this matter and do not be followers in it; be first in it and do not be last in it."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat* narrated from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾: he said, "It is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and *ihsan* (excellence) is the performance of the obligations." ﴿And giving to kinsmen﴾: he said, "Giving to the near of kin the right that Allah has made obligatory upon you by reason of kinship and the ties of blood." ﴿And He forbids indecency﴾: he said, "Fornication and the reprehensible." [He said] "*al-munkar*": he said, "Shirk (associating partners with Allah) and transgression." [He said] "*al-baghy*": he said, "Pride and oppression." ﴿He admonishes you﴾: he said, "He enjoins you." ﴿So that you may remember﴾.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Bukhari in *al-Adab*, Muhammad ibn Nasr in *al-Salat*, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in *Shu'ab al-Iman* narrated that he said: "The greatest verse in the Book of Allah is ﴿Allah, there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:255]. The most comprehensive verse in the Book of Allah for good and evil is the verse in al-Nahl ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾. The verse in the Book of Allah most full of *tafwid* (entrusting one's affairs to Allah) is ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [al-Talaq 65:2–3]. The most intense verse in the Book of Allah in hope is ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ [al-Zumar 39:53], [and so on] to the end of the verse."

Al-Bayhaqi in *Shu'ab al-Iman* narrated from al-Hasan that he recited this verse ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾ to its end, then said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has gathered for you all good and all evil in one verse. By Allah, justice and excellence have left out nothing of obedience to Allah without including it, and indecency, the reprehensible, and transgression have left out nothing of disobedience to Allah without including it."

Al-Bukhari in his *Tarikh* narrated through al-Kalbi from his father, who said: "Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by a people who were conversing and said, 'What are you discussing?' They said, 'We are discussing *al-muru'ah* (manliness and chivalrous conduct).' He said, 'Has Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not sufficed you with that in His Book when He says: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾? Justice is equity, and excellence is generosity beyond what is due. What remains after this?'"

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 16, verses 84–90 (part 1 of 2):

He said: ﴿And [mention] the Day when We raise up from every nation a witness﴾. That is, mention the Day when We raise up, or [it means]: the Day when We raise up, they will fall into what they fell into. The witness of every nation is its prophet, who testifies for them to faith and affirmation, and against them to disbelief, denial and rejection. ﴿Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved﴾, that is, to make excuses, since they have no proof and no excuse, as in His statement, glory be to Him: ﴿Nor will they be permitted, so they could make excuse﴾ [al-Mursalat: 36]. Or [it means]: to speak at length. Or: to return to the worldly abode. The use of "then" (thumma) here indicates that their being afflicted with being prevented from making excuses, which indicates total despair, is more severe than their being afflicted with the testimony of the prophets. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾, because reproach (`itab) is only sought for the purpose of returning to good pleasure; so when there is a resolve of wrath, there is no benefit in reproach.

The meaning: they will not be asked to be pleased, that is, they will not be required to please their Lord, because the Hereafter is not an abode of obligation, and they will not be left to return to the world so that they might repent. The root of the word is from `atab, which means "to be aggrieved." It is said: `atiba `alayhi, ya`tibu, when he was aggrieved with him. When he pours upon him what he was aggrieved about, it is said `atabahu (he reproached him). When he returns to his gladness, it is said a`tabahu (he appeased him). The noun is al-`utba, which is the return of the one who was reproached to what pleases the reproacher. Al-Harawi said this, and from it is the saying of al-Nabigha:

"If I am wronged, [it is] a slave whom you have wronged; and if I have grievance, one like you appeases."

﴿And when those who wronged see the punishment﴾, that is, when those who associated partners [with God] see the punishment that they deserve for their polytheism, which is the punishment of Hell, that punishment will not be lightened for them ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾, that is, they will not be given respite to repent, since there is no repentance there.

﴿And when those who associated partners see their partners﴾, that is, their idols and images which they worshipped, because it has been established that they will be raised together with the polytheists, so that it will be said to them: "Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it," as established in the Sahih from the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿They will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You."﴾ That is, those whom we used to worship besides You.

Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: The intent of the polytheists in this statement is to shift the blame onto those idols, making excuses and seeking relief by it, while knowing that the punishment is inevitably befalling them; but the drowning person clutches at whatever his hand falls upon. ﴿Then they will throw to them the word﴾, that is, those idols, images, devils and the like will cast to the polytheists the word ﴿"Indeed, you are liars."﴾ That is, they will say to them: "Indeed you, O polytheists, are liars in what you claim of shifting the blame onto us, which is your intent in this statement."

Then he said to his people: "Be leaders in this matter and do not be followers in it; be first in it and do not be last in it."

[He said] "*al-munkar*": he said, "Shirk (associating partners with Allah) and transgression." [He said] "*al-baghy*": he said, "Pride and oppression." ﴿He admonishes you﴾: he said, "He enjoins you." ﴿So that you may remember﴾.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Bukhari in *al-Adab*, Muhammad ibn Nasr in *al-Salat*, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in *Shu'ab al-Iman* narrated that he said: "The greatest verse in the Book of Allah is ﴿Allah, there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:255]. The most comprehensive verse in the Book of Allah for good and evil is the verse in al-Nahl ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾. The verse in the Book of Allah most full of *tafwid* (entrusting one's affairs to Allah) is ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [al-Talaq 65:2–3]. The most intense verse in the Book of Allah in hope is ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ [al-Zumar 39:53], [and so on] to the end of the verse."

Al-Bayhaqi in *Shu'ab al-Iman* narrated from al-Hasan that he recited this verse ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾ to its end, then said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has gathered for you all good and all evil in one verse. By Allah, justice and excellence have left out nothing of obedience to Allah without including it, and indecency, the reprehensible, and transgression have left out nothing of disobedience to Allah without including it."

Al-Bukhari in his *Tarikh* narrated through al-Kalbi from his father, who said: "Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by a people who were conversing and said, 'What are you discussing?' They said, 'We are discussing *al-muru'ah* (manliness and chivalrous conduct).' He said, 'Has Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not sufficed you with that in His Book when He says: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾? Justice is equity, and excellence is generosity beyond what is due. What remains after this?'"

Allah, glorified is He, singled out from among the matters commanded in His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾, the fulfilment of covenants, and said: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have made it﴾. Its apparent meaning is general, covering every covenant a person makes, without distinguishing between the covenant of allegiance (bay'ah) and others. Some exegetes restricted the covenant mentioned in this verse to the covenant of the Prophet's ﷺ allegiance to Islam. This contradicts what the covenant attributed to the name of Allah, glorified is He, indicates of generality, encompassing all of Allah's covenants. Even if it were supposed that the occasion of revelation was specific to one particular covenant, that would not require restricting the ruling to that occasion. The consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion. Some exegetes interpreted it as referring to oaths (yamin), but this is refuted by the mention after it of fulfilling oaths, where He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and do not break your oaths after their confirmation﴾, meaning after their strengthening, their emphasis and their solemnisation. The intended meaning is not that the prohibition of breaking oaths applies only to emphatic oaths and not to others in which there is no emphasis, for the prohibition of breaking [an oath] encompasses all of them. Rather, breaking an emphatic oath carries greater sin than breaking one that is not emphasised. It is said: wakkada and akkada, with the tawkid and ta'kid, and both are two dialects.

Al-Zajjaj said: The original root is waw, and the hamzah replaces it. This generality is specified by what is established in the sound hadiths of his saying ﷺ: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something else as better than it, let him do what is better and make expiation (kaffarah) for his oath." He ﷺ went so far in this that he said: "By Allah, I will not swear an oath and then see something else as better than it, except that I will do what is better and make expiation for my oath." These wordings are established in the Two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim, the two authentic collections) and others. Also specified from this generality is the idle oath (yamin al-laghw), by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Allah does not hold you accountable for the idle [oaths] in your oaths﴾ (al-Baqarah 225; al-Ma'idah 89). It is possible that the restriction to emphasis here is to exclude idle oaths. The discussion of oaths has already been fully expounded in al-Baqarah.

﴿And you have made Allah your guarantor (kafil)﴾, meaning a witness; it was said a guardian; it was said a surety; it was said an overseer, because the guarantor watches over the condition of the one guaranteed. It was also said that the emphasis of an oath is a person swearing on one matter several times.

Al-Qurtubi related from Ibn 'Umar that the emphasis is that one swears twice; if he swears once, there is no expiation for him. ﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you do﴾, so He will reward you according to that: if it is good, then good; if it is evil, then evil. In this is both encouragement and warning.

Then He affirmed the obligation of fulfilment and the prohibition of breaking [covenants], saying: ﴿And do not be like her who unravelled her spun thread﴾, meaning: do not be, in what you do of breaking after emphasis, like her who unravelled her thread, that is, what she had spun after strength, that is, after the spun thread had been twisted firm and made strong. This is connected to ﴿unravelled﴾. ﴿Into pieces (ankathan)﴾ is the plural of nikth, with a kasrah on the nun, meaning that which has been untwisted.

Al-Zajjaj said: ankathan is in the accusative as an infinitive (masdar), because the meaning of naqadat is nakathat. This was refuted on the grounds that ankathan is not an infinitive but a plural, as we have mentioned.

Al-Wahidi said: it is in the accusative as a second object, as you say "I broke it into pieces (aqta' an) and parts (ajza')", meaning "I made it into pieces and parts". It may also be a circumstantial accusative (hal).

Ibn Qutaybah said: this verse is connected to what precedes it, and the implied meaning is: "Fulfil the covenant of Allah and do not break the oaths, for if you do that you will be like a woman who spun thread, made it firm, and then made it into pieces." The clause ﴿taking your oaths as deception (dakhal) among yourselves﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause.

Al-Jawhari said: al-dakhal is deceit and trickery. Abu 'Ubaydah said: everything that is not sound is dakhal.

It was said: al-dakhal is what is introduced into a thing to corrupt it.

Al-Zajjaj said: [it means] deceit and malice.

﴿Lest one community be more numerous than another community﴾, meaning: that one group should be more numerous than another group, that is, greater in number and richer in wealth. It is said: "rabā al-shay'u yarbū" when it increases.

Al-Farra' said: the meaning is: do not betray a people because of your fewness and their multitude, or because of your multitude and their fewness, when you have already strengthened them with oaths.

It was said: Quraysh, when they saw strength among the enemies of their allies, would break their covenant and form alliances with their enemies. It was also said that this is a warning to the believers not to be deceived by the multitude of Quraysh and the abundance of their wealth, and so break the allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿Allah only tests you thereby﴾, meaning He tests you by your being more numerous and more wealthy, to see whether you hold fast to the rope of fulfilment or break [it] out of deception by multitude? So the pronoun in "thereby" refers to the content of the clause ﴿that one community be more numerous than another community﴾. That is: Allah only tests you with that multitude in order to know what you do. Or: Allah only tests you with what He commands you and forbids you. ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ﴾, so He will clarify the truth and those who uphold it and raise their ranks, and make clear falsehood and those who uphold it, and bring upon them the punishment they deserve. In this is a warning and admonition against opposing the truth and inclining towards falsehood. Or it makes clear to you what you used to differ about concerning resurrection, Paradise and Hell.

Then He, glorified is He, made clear that He is able to unite the believers and the disbelievers in fulfilment or in faith, saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community﴾, agreed upon the truth. But by the judgement of His divinity, ﴿He leaves astray whom He wills﴾, by forsaking them, as justice from Him toward them, ﴿and guides whom He wills﴾, by granting them success, as grace from Him upon them. ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ (al-Anbiya' 23). For this reason He said: ﴿And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do﴾ of deeds in this world. The lam in ﴿and He will surely make clear to you﴾ and in ﴿and you will surely be questioned﴾ are both the preparatory lams (al-muwatti'atan) for the oath.

Then, when He, glorified is He, forbade breaking oaths in general, He forbade breaking particular oaths, saying: ﴿And do not take your oaths as deception among yourselves﴾, and these are the oaths of allegiance (bay'ah).

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: this is in the prohibition of those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from breaking the covenant of Islam and support of the religion. They cited as evidence for this restriction what is in His saying: ﴿lest a foot slip after its firmness﴾ of emphasis, and what is in His saying: ﴿and taste evil for what you have averted﴾, because when they broke the covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ they averted others from entering Islam.

And even granting that these oaths with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were the occasion of revelation of this verse, the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion.

A group of exegetes said: This is a repetition of what precedes it for the purpose of emphasis and affirmation. The meaning of ﴿lest a foot slip after its firmness﴾ is: lest the foot of one who took his oath as deception slip from the right path after it had been firm upon it and established in it.

It was said: The singular "foot" is used to indicate that the slipping of a single foot, whichever foot it is, whether it was firm or weak, is a great danger; so how much more so with many feet? This is a metaphor for one who is in a sound condition who falls into great evil and collapses into it, because when a foot slips it moves a person from a state of good to a state of evil. It is said of one who erred in something: his foot slipped. From this is the poet's saying:

"You two have sought out 'Abs, though its throne has been shattered, and Dhibyan's sandals have slipped on their feet."

﴿And taste evil for what you have averted﴾, meaning: taste the evil punishment in this world or in the Hereafter, or in both, for what you averted ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, that is, because of your own averting from the way of Allah, which is Islam, or because of your averting others from Islam. For whoever breaks allegiance and apostatises, others follow him in that, so his act becomes an evil sunnah (precedent), bearing its burden and the burden of those who act upon it. For this reason He said: ﴿And for you is a great punishment﴾, meaning one extremely great in magnitude, which is the punishment of the Hereafter, if what is meant by what precedes it is the punishment of this world.

Then He, glorified is He, forbade them from inclining toward the transient goods of this world and from retracting the covenant for its sake, saying: ﴿And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price﴾, meaning: do not take in exchange for your covenant a small, insignificant compensation. Every worldly good, even if it appears abundant in form, is, because it is passing and fleeting, small. For this reason, after diminishing the goods of this world, He, glorified is He, mentioned the superiority of what is with Allah, saying: ﴿Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you﴾, meaning: what He has of victory in this world, spoils, and abundant provision, and what He has in the Hereafter of the bliss of Paradise, which does not cease or end, is better for them. Then He explained the prohibition against exchanging the covenant of Allah for a small price, and that what is with Allah is better for them, by His saying: ﴿if you only knew﴾, meaning if you are among the people of knowledge and discernment between things.

Then He mentioned a decisive proof of the worthlessness of the goods of this world and the superiority of what is with Allah, saying: ﴿What you have will be exhausted, but what is with Allah will remain﴾. It is known to every intelligent person that what is exhausted and passes away, however great its quantity may reach, is petty and small; and what remains and does not pass away is abundant and magnificent. As for the bliss of the Hereafter, it is evident. As for the bliss of this world with which Allah has favoured the believers, although it passes away, since it is connected to the bliss of the Hereafter, it is, from this standpoint, in the ruling of what remains and does not end. Then He said: ﴿And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾. The lam is the preparatory lam, meaning: We will surely reward them, on account of their patience in what befell them of the hardships of obligation and striving against the disbelievers, and their patience in what they suffered from them of harm, according to the best of what they used to do of acts of obedience.

It was said: He specified their best deeds because what is other than that, which is good, is permissible, and reward is only for obedience. It was also said that the meaning is: We will reward them with a reward more noble and abundant than their deeds, as in His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ (al-An'am 160). Or: We will reward them according to the best individual forms of their deeds, meaning: We will give them, in return for the lowest individual of their mentioned deeds, what We give them in return for the highest individual of them of great reward; not that We give the reward according to the variation of their individual forms in degrees of goodness, such that We reward the good among them with good reward and the best with the best. Thus it was said.

ʿĀṣim and Ibn Kathīr read "la-najziyannahum" with the nun.

The rest read it with the yā' (third person).

[p. 801] Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿and do not break the oaths after their affirmation﴾, that he said: after their strengthening.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related the same from Qatadah.

Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Ibn Mardawayh related through the chain of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Sa'idah al-Asadiyyah used to gather hair and fibre, and this verse was revealed concerning her: ﴿and do not be like her who unravelled her spun thread﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from Abu Bakr ibn Hafs, and in both reports together it is stated that she was insane.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi concerning the occasion of revelation of the verse, that he said: There was a woman in Mecca called "the foolish woman of Mecca" who used to spin, and when she had twisted her thread firmly, she would unravel it.

Ibn Jarir related from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir the same meaning.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿lest one community be more numerous than another community﴾, that he said: some people are more numerous than some people.

They also related from Mujahid concerning the verse, that he said: They used to form alliances with allies, then they would find others more numerous and more powerful than them, so they would break the alliance with these and ally themselves with those who were more powerful, so they were forbidden from that.

Allah, glorified is He, singled out from among the matters commanded in His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾, the fulfilment of covenants, and said: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have made it﴾. Its apparent meaning is general, covering every covenant a person makes, without distinguishing between the covenant of allegiance (bay'ah) and others. Some exegetes restricted the covenant mentioned in this verse to the covenant of the Prophet's ﷺ allegiance to Islam. This contradicts what the covenant attributed to the name of Allah, glorified is He, indicates of generality, encompassing all of Allah's covenants. Even if it were supposed that the occasion of revelation was specific to one particular covenant, that would not require restricting the ruling to that occasion. The consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion. Some exegetes interpreted it as referring to oaths (yamin), but this is refuted by the mention after it of fulfilling oaths, where He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and do not break your oaths after their confirmation﴾, meaning after their strengthening, their emphasis and their solemnisation. The intended meaning is not that the prohibition of breaking oaths applies only to emphatic oaths and not to others in which there is no emphasis, for the prohibition of breaking [an oath] encompasses all of them. Rather, breaking an emphatic oath carries greater sin than breaking one that is not emphasised. It is said: wakkada and akkada, with the tawkid and ta'kid, and both are two dialects.

Al-Zajjaj said: The original root is waw, and the hamzah replaces it. This generality is specified by what is established in the sound hadiths of his saying ﷺ: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something else as better than it, let him do what is better and make expiation (kaffarah) for his oath." He ﷺ went so far in this that he said: "By Allah, I will not swear an oath and then see something else as better than it, except that I will do what is better and make expiation for my oath." These wordings are established in the Two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim, the two authentic collections) and others. Also specified from this generality is the idle oath (yamin al-laghw), by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Allah does not hold you accountable for the idle [oaths] in your oaths﴾ (al-Baqarah 225; al-Ma'idah 89). It is possible that the restriction to emphasis here is to exclude idle oaths. The discussion of oaths has already been fully expounded in al-Baqarah.

﴿And you have made Allah your guarantor (kafil)﴾, meaning a witness; it was said a guardian; it was said a surety; it was said an overseer, because the guarantor watches over the condition of the one guaranteed. It was also said that the emphasis of an oath is a person swearing on one matter several times.

Al-Qurtubi related from Ibn 'Umar that the emphasis is that one swears twice; if he swears once, there is no expiation for him. ﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you do﴾, so He will reward you according to that: if it is good, then good; if it is evil, then evil. In this is both encouragement and warning.

Then He affirmed the obligation of fulfilment and the prohibition of breaking [covenants], saying: ﴿And do not be like her who unravelled her spun thread﴾, meaning: do not be, in what you do of breaking after emphasis, like her who unravelled her thread, that is, what she had spun after strength, that is, after the spun thread had been twisted firm and made strong. This is connected to ﴿unravelled﴾. ﴿Into pieces (ankathan)﴾ is the plural of nikth, with a kasrah on the nun, meaning that which has been untwisted.

Al-Zajjaj said: ankathan is in the accusative as an infinitive (masdar), because the meaning of naqadat is nakathat. This was refuted on the grounds that ankathan is not an infinitive but a plural, as we have mentioned.

Al-Wahidi said: it is in the accusative as a second object, as you say "I broke it into pieces (aqta' an) and parts (ajza')", meaning "I made it into pieces and parts". It may also be a circumstantial accusative (hal).

Ibn Qutaybah said: this verse is connected to what precedes it, and the implied meaning is: "Fulfil the covenant of Allah and do not break the oaths, for if you do that you will be like a woman who spun thread, made it firm, and then made it into pieces." The clause ﴿taking your oaths as deception (dakhal) among yourselves﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause.

Al-Jawhari said: al-dakhal is deceit and trickery. Abu 'Ubaydah said: everything that is not sound is dakhal.

It was said: al-dakhal is what is introduced into a thing to corrupt it.

Al-Zajjaj said: [it means] deceit and malice.

﴿Lest one community be more numerous than another community﴾, meaning: that one group should be more numerous than another group, that is, greater in number and richer in wealth. It is said: "rabā al-shay'u yarbū" when it increases.

Al-Farra' said: the meaning is: do not betray a people because of your fewness and their multitude, or because of your multitude and their fewness, when you have already strengthened them with oaths.

It was said: Quraysh, when they saw strength among the enemies of their allies, would break their covenant and form alliances with their enemies. It was also said that this is a warning to the believers not to be deceived by the multitude of Quraysh and the abundance of their wealth, and so break the allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿Allah only tests you thereby﴾, meaning He tests you by your being more numerous and more wealthy, to see whether you hold fast to the rope of fulfilment or break [it] out of deception by multitude? So the pronoun in "thereby" refers to the content of the clause ﴿that one community be more numerous than another community﴾. That is: Allah only tests you with that multitude in order to know what you do. Or: Allah only tests you with what He commands you and forbids you. ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ﴾, so He will clarify the truth and those who uphold it and raise their ranks, and make clear falsehood and those who uphold it, and bring upon them the punishment they deserve. In this is a warning and admonition against opposing the truth and inclining towards falsehood. Or it makes clear to you what you used to differ about concerning resurrection, Paradise and Hell.

Then He, glorified is He, made clear that He is able to unite the believers and the disbelievers in fulfilment or in faith, saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community﴾, agreed upon the truth. But by the judgement of His divinity, ﴿He leaves astray whom He wills﴾, by forsaking them, as justice from Him toward them, ﴿and guides whom He wills﴾, by granting them success, as grace from Him upon them. ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ (al-Anbiya' 23). For this reason He said: ﴿And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do﴾ of deeds in this world. The lam in ﴿and He will surely make clear to you﴾ and in ﴿and you will surely be questioned﴾ are both the preparatory lams (al-muwatti'atan) for the oath.

Then, when He, glorified is He, forbade breaking oaths in general, He forbade breaking particular oaths, saying: ﴿And do not take your oaths as deception among yourselves﴾, and these are the oaths of allegiance (bay'ah).

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: this is in the prohibition of those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from breaking the covenant of Islam and support of the religion. They cited as evidence for this restriction what is in His saying: ﴿lest a foot slip after its firmness﴾ of emphasis, and what is in His saying: ﴿and taste evil for what you have averted﴾, because when they broke the covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ they averted others from entering Islam.

And even granting that these oaths with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were the occasion of revelation of this verse, the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion.

A group of exegetes said: This is a repetition of what precedes it for the purpose of emphasis and affirmation. The meaning of ﴿lest a foot slip after its firmness﴾ is: lest the foot of one who took his oath as deception slip from the right path after it had been firm upon it and established in it.

It was said: The singular "foot" is used to indicate that the slipping of a single foot, whichever foot it is, whether it was firm or weak, is a great danger; so how much more so with many feet? This is a metaphor for one who is in a sound condition who falls into great evil and collapses into it, because when a foot slips it moves a person from a state of good to a state of evil. It is said of one who erred in something: his foot slipped. From this is the poet's saying:

"You two have sought out 'Abs, though its throne has been shattered, and Dhibyan's sandals have slipped on their feet."

﴿And taste evil for what you have averted﴾, meaning: taste the evil punishment in this world or in the Hereafter, or in both, for what you averted ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, that is, because of your own averting from the way of Allah, which is Islam, or because of your averting others from Islam. For whoever breaks allegiance and apostatises, others follow him in that, so his act becomes an evil sunnah (precedent), bearing its burden and the burden of those who act upon it. For this reason He said: ﴿And for you is a great punishment﴾, meaning one extremely great in magnitude, which is the punishment of the Hereafter, if what is meant by what precedes it is the punishment of this world.

Then He, glorified is He, forbade them from inclining toward the transient goods of this world and from retracting the covenant for its sake, saying: ﴿And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price﴾, meaning: do not take in exchange for your covenant a small, insignificant compensation. Every worldly good, even if it appears abundant in form, is, because it is passing and fleeting, small. For this reason, after diminishing the goods of this world, He, glorified is He, mentioned the superiority of what is with Allah, saying: ﴿Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you﴾, meaning: what He has of victory in this world, spoils, and abundant provision, and what He has in the Hereafter of the bliss of Paradise, which does not cease or end, is better for them. Then He explained the prohibition against exchanging the covenant of Allah for a small price, and that what is with Allah is better for them, by His saying: ﴿if you only knew﴾, meaning if you are among the people of knowledge and discernment between things.

Then He mentioned a decisive proof of the worthlessness of the goods of this world and the superiority of what is with Allah, saying: ﴿What you have will be exhausted, but what is with Allah will remain﴾. It is known to every intelligent person that what is exhausted and passes away, however great its quantity may reach, is petty and small; and what remains and does not pass away is abundant and magnificent. As for the bliss of the Hereafter, it is evident. As for the bliss of this world with which Allah has favoured the believers, although it passes away, since it is connected to the bliss of the Hereafter, it is, from this standpoint, in the ruling of what remains and does not end. Then He said: ﴿And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾. The lam is the preparatory lam, meaning: We will surely reward them, on account of their patience in what befell them of the hardships of obligation and striving against the disbelievers, and their patience in what they suffered from them of harm, according to the best of what they used to do of acts of obedience.

It was said: He specified their best deeds because what is other than that, which is good, is permissible, and reward is only for obedience. It was also said that the meaning is: We will reward them with a reward more noble and abundant than their deeds, as in His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ (al-An'am 160). Or: We will reward them according to the best individual forms of their deeds, meaning: We will give them, in return for the lowest individual of their mentioned deeds, what We give them in return for the highest individual of them of great reward; not that We give the reward according to the variation of their individual forms in degrees of goodness, such that We reward the good among them with good reward and the best with the best. Thus it was said.

The rest read it with the yā' (third person).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿lest one community be more numerous than another community﴾, that he said: some people are more numerous than some people.

They also related from Mujahid concerning the verse, that he said: They used to form alliances with allies, then they would find others more numerous and more powerful than them, so they would break the alliance with these and ally themselves with those who were more powerful, so they were forbidden from that.

Allah, glorified is He, singled out from among the matters commanded in His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾, the fulfilment of covenants, and said: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have made it﴾. Its apparent meaning is general, covering every covenant a person makes, without distinguishing between the covenant of allegiance (bay'ah) and others. Some exegetes restricted the covenant mentioned in this verse to the covenant of the Prophet's ﷺ allegiance to Islam. This contradicts what the covenant attributed to the name of Allah, glorified is He, indicates of generality, encompassing all of Allah's covenants. Even if it were supposed that the occasion of revelation was specific to one particular covenant, that would not require restricting the ruling to that occasion. The consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion. Some exegetes interpreted it as referring to oaths (yamin), but this is refuted by the mention after it of fulfilling oaths, where He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and do not break your oaths after their confirmation﴾, meaning after their strengthening, their emphasis and their solemnisation. The intended meaning is not that the prohibition of breaking oaths applies only to emphatic oaths and not to others in which there is no emphasis, for the prohibition of breaking [an oath] encompasses all of them. Rather, breaking an emphatic oath carries greater sin than breaking one that is not emphasised. It is said: wakkada and akkada, with the tawkid and ta'kid, and both are two dialects.

Al-Zajjaj said: The original root is waw, and the hamzah replaces it. This generality is specified by what is established in the sound hadiths of his saying ﷺ: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees something else as better than it, let him do what is better and make expiation (kaffarah) for his oath." He ﷺ went so far in this that he said: "By Allah, I will not swear an oath and then see something else as better than it, except that I will do what is better and make expiation for my oath." These wordings are established in the Two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim, the two authentic collections) and others. Also specified from this generality is the idle oath (yamin al-laghw), by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Allah does not hold you accountable for the idle [oaths] in your oaths﴾ (al-Baqarah 225; al-Ma'idah 89). It is possible that the restriction to emphasis here is to exclude idle oaths. The discussion of oaths has already been fully expounded in al-Baqarah.

﴿And you have made Allah your guarantor (kafil)﴾, meaning a witness; it was said a guardian; it was said a surety; it was said an overseer, because the guarantor watches over the condition of the one guaranteed. It was also said that the emphasis of an oath is a person swearing on one matter several times.

Al-Qurtubi related from Ibn 'Umar that the emphasis is that one swears twice; if he swears once, there is no expiation for him. ﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you do﴾, so He will reward you according to that: if it is good, then good; if it is evil, then evil. In this is both encouragement and warning.

Then He affirmed the obligation of fulfilment and the prohibition of breaking [covenants], saying: ﴿And do not be like her who unravelled her spun thread﴾, meaning: do not be, in what you do of breaking after emphasis, like her who unravelled her thread, that is, what she had spun after strength, that is, after the spun thread had been twisted firm and made strong. This is connected to ﴿unravelled﴾. ﴿Into pieces (ankathan)﴾ is the plural of nikth, with a kasrah on the nun, meaning that which has been untwisted.

Al-Zajjaj said: ankathan is in the accusative as an infinitive (masdar), because the meaning of naqadat is nakathat. This was refuted on the grounds that ankathan is not an infinitive but a plural, as we have mentioned.

Al-Wahidi said: it is in the accusative as a second object, as you say "I broke it into pieces (aqta' an) and parts (ajza')", meaning "I made it into pieces and parts". It may also be a circumstantial accusative (hal).

Ibn Qutaybah said: this verse is connected to what precedes it, and the implied meaning is: "Fulfil the covenant of Allah and do not break the oaths, for if you do that you will be like a woman who spun thread, made it firm, and then made it into pieces." The clause ﴿taking your oaths as deception (dakhal) among yourselves﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause.

Al-Jawhari said: al-dakhal is deceit and trickery. Abu 'Ubaydah said: everything that is not sound is dakhal.

It was said: al-dakhal is what is introduced into a thing to corrupt it.

Al-Zajjaj said: [it means] deceit and malice.

﴿Lest one community be more numerous than another community﴾, meaning: that one group should be more numerous than another group, that is, greater in number and richer in wealth. It is said: "rabā al-shay'u yarbū" when it increases.

Al-Farra' said: the meaning is: do not betray a people because of your fewness and their multitude, or because of your multitude and their fewness, when you have already strengthened them with oaths.

It was said: Quraysh, when they saw strength among the enemies of their allies, would break their covenant and form alliances with their enemies. It was also said that this is a warning to the believers not to be deceived by the multitude of Quraysh and the abundance of their wealth, and so break the allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿Allah only tests you thereby﴾, meaning He tests you by your being more numerous and more wealthy, to see whether you hold fast to the rope of fulfilment or break [it] out of deception by multitude? So the pronoun in "thereby" refers to the content of the clause ﴿that one community be more numerous than another community﴾. That is: Allah only tests you with that multitude in order to know what you do. Or: Allah only tests you with what He commands you and forbids you. ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ﴾, so He will clarify the truth and those who uphold it and raise their ranks, and make clear falsehood and those who uphold it, and bring upon them the punishment they deserve. In this is a warning and admonition against opposing the truth and inclining towards falsehood. Or it makes clear to you what you used to differ about concerning resurrection, Paradise and Hell.

Then He, glorified is He, made clear that He is able to unite the believers and the disbelievers in fulfilment or in faith, saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one community﴾, agreed upon the truth. But by the judgement of His divinity, ﴿He leaves astray whom He wills﴾, by forsaking them, as justice from Him toward them, ﴿and guides whom He wills﴾, by granting them success, as grace from Him upon them. ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ (al-Anbiya' 23). For this reason He said: ﴿And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do﴾ of deeds in this world. The lam in ﴿and He will surely make clear to you﴾ and in ﴿and you will surely be questioned﴾ are both the preparatory lams (al-muwatti'atan) for the oath.

Then, when He, glorified is He, forbade breaking oaths in general, He forbade breaking particular oaths, saying: ﴿And do not take your oaths as deception among yourselves﴾, and these are the oaths of allegiance (bay'ah).

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: this is in the prohibition of those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from breaking the covenant of Islam and support of the religion. They cited as evidence for this restriction what is in His saying: ﴿lest a foot slip after its firmness﴾ of emphasis, and what is in His saying: ﴿and taste evil for what you have averted﴾, because when they broke the covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ they averted others from entering Islam.

And even granting that these oaths with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were the occasion of revelation of this verse, the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion.

A group of exegetes said: This is a repetition of what precedes it for the purpose of emphasis and affirmation. The meaning of ﴿lest a foot slip after its firmness﴾ is: lest the foot of one who took his oath as deception slip from the right path after it had been firm upon it and established in it.

It was said: The singular "foot" is used to indicate that the slipping of a single foot, whichever foot it is, whether it was firm or weak, is a great danger; so how much more so with many feet? This is a metaphor for one who is in a sound condition who falls into great evil and collapses into it, because when a foot slips it moves a person from a state of good to a state of evil. It is said of one who erred in something: his foot slipped. From this is the poet's saying:

"You two have sought out 'Abs, though its throne has been shattered, and Dhibyan's sandals have slipped on their feet."

﴿And taste evil for what you have averted﴾, meaning: taste the evil punishment in this world or in the Hereafter, or in both, for what you averted ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, that is, because of your own averting from the way of Allah, which is Islam, or because of your averting others from Islam. For whoever breaks allegiance and apostatises, others follow him in that, so his act becomes an evil sunnah (precedent), bearing its burden and the burden of those who act upon it. For this reason He said: ﴿And for you is a great punishment﴾, meaning one extremely great in magnitude, which is the punishment of the Hereafter, if what is meant by what precedes it is the punishment of this world.

Then He, glorified is He, forbade them from inclining toward the transient goods of this world and from retracting the covenant for its sake, saying: ﴿And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price﴾, meaning: do not take in exchange for your covenant a small, insignificant compensation. Every worldly good, even if it appears abundant in form, is, because it is passing and fleeting, small. For this reason, after diminishing the goods of this world, He, glorified is He, mentioned the superiority of what is with Allah, saying: ﴿Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you﴾, meaning: what He has of victory in this world, spoils, and abundant provision, and what He has in the Hereafter of the bliss of Paradise, which does not cease or end, is better for them. Then He explained the prohibition against exchanging the covenant of Allah for a small price, and that what is with Allah is better for them, by His saying: ﴿if you only knew﴾, meaning if you are among the people of knowledge and discernment between things.

Then He mentioned a decisive proof of the worthlessness of the goods of this world and the superiority of what is with Allah, saying: ﴿What you have will be exhausted, but what is with Allah will remain﴾. It is known to every intelligent person that what is exhausted and passes away, however great its quantity may reach, is petty and small; and what remains and does not pass away is abundant and magnificent. As for the bliss of the Hereafter, it is evident. As for the bliss of this world with which Allah has favoured the believers, although it passes away, since it is connected to the bliss of the Hereafter, it is, from this standpoint, in the ruling of what remains and does not end. Then He said: ﴿And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾. The lam is the preparatory lam, meaning: We will surely reward them, on account of their patience in what befell them of the hardships of obligation and striving against the disbelievers, and their patience in what they suffered from them of harm, according to the best of what they used to do of acts of obedience.

It was said: He specified their best deeds because what is other than that, which is good, is permissible, and reward is only for obedience. It was also said that the meaning is: We will reward them with a reward more noble and abundant than their deeds, as in His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ (al-An'am 160). Or: We will reward them according to the best individual forms of their deeds, meaning: We will give them, in return for the lowest individual of their mentioned deeds, what We give them in return for the highest individual of them of great reward; not that We give the reward according to the variation of their individual forms in degrees of goodness, such that We reward the good among them with good reward and the best with the best. Thus it was said.
